1	# Speed ramps: a clip's rate changing over time, as a Speed action (road map "speed-ramps")
2	
3	- **Status:** Built and closed 2026-10-24, for #111. Each phase was one litecode pipeline with its own review, worked in `~/devel/framejob-ramps` on branch `speed-ramps` and merged into main alone after its gate (SR-4). Five of them were spikes, each judged by a rule fixed before its run:
4	  - SR1, the road map, SR-1…SR-5 and the segment spike: STOP (`ffcb4b5`)
5	  - SR1b, the rendered-audio spike (SR-6, SR-7): SPLIT, off GO, on STOP (`874ecc8`)
6	  - SR1c, Keep pitch as resample, then pitch-shift (SR-8, SR-9): STOP (`214aee8`)
7	  - SR2a, `speed` as an action target, the speed map and the plan (SR-10, SR-11; format 27) (`2ee4e34`)
8	  - SR2b, the render wired into playback and export (SR-12) (`a579f71`), after its toll, `CompositionBuilder+Orientation.swift` (`5042934`)
9	  - SR1d, Keep pitch through Apple's time-pitch in rate mode with a 56 ms lead (SR-13…SR-15): STOP, landed on the owner's answer (`242f104`)
10	  - SR1e, the closed loop measured and closed (SR-16, SR-17) (`e2e79b9`)
11	  - SR3a, trims, roll, slip, split, freeze and the handle on a ramped clip (SR-18) (`27bbe72`)
12	  - SR3b, rate edits scale the whole profile; copies and re-snaps carry a ramp (SR-19) (`d35c716`)
13	  - SR4, Swift's mappers (SR-20) (`6a1b7a9`), after its toll, `CoreValues.swift` and `ReelOpSchema.swift` (`0b4be0b`)
14	  - SR5, the UI and #338 (SR-21, SR-22) (`6d1a968`), after its toll, `InspectorLabels.swift` (`a572d3f`)
15	  - The close: this record (the commit that moved the original to `archive/`)
16	- **Original:** `archive/speed-ramps.md` is the full record. It has no section numbers, so it is cited by its own headings: "orig SR2b" is its "SR2b — the renderer wired in" section, and "orig rule I" is the rule I bullet of its "Decided here".
17	- **Spec decisions:** SR-1..SR-22 in spec §11: SR-1…SR-12 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/speed-ramps.md`, SR-13…SR-22 in `speed-ramps-2.md` (split at the close by the spec's ~500-line rule). They stay binding, and where the original words them differently, §11's text wins:
18	  - SR-1: a speed ramp is a Speed action on the action lane, ramping from the rate in force to its end rate along its curve and held after.
19	  - SR-2: the clip keeps its slot; a ramp changes how much source it plays, and an edit reading past the media's end is refused, naming the rate or end that fits.
20	  - SR-3: audio follows the clip's own Keep pitch, with no time-stretch of Frame Job's own (SY-41).
21	  - SR-4: the working arrangement: the worktree, each phase gated and merged alone, synthetic fixtures, no `--live` run, owner media never read.
22	  - SR-5: the segment spike's rule: abutting constant-rate segments every G frames, judged for placement, click, dropout, video and agreement, and a verdict of GO, GO-UNIFORM-LEAD, GO-EXPORT-ONLY or STOP.
23	  - SR-6: a ramped clip's audio is rendered offline into `cache/ramp-audio/` and carried as one ×1 segment; with Keep pitch off, a Kaiser-windowed-sinc tape glide.
24	  - SR-7: the rendered-audio spike's rule: placement against the ideal map, a dense click scan, PT1's ×1 tap correction and a verdict per Keep pitch arm.
25	  - SR-8: Keep pitch on as resample, then pitch-shift (superseded whole by SR-13).
26	  - SR-9: the third spike's rule: SR-7's arm ON plus the rendered pitch and its lag.
27	  - SR-10: `end.speed`, the rate rule, S in closed form, per-frame video segments placed as one unit, one audio segment carrying the map, the slot's refusals and format 27.
28	  - SR-11: Keep pitch inside a ramp glided like tape as an interim (lifted by SR-13 and SR-15).
29	  - SR-12: the render wired in: a file per plan ramp segment, ready iff it exists, owners and one serial queue, the landing under the cache ledger, the export's wait.
30	  - SR-13: Keep pitch on is `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` in rate mode, its rate commanded `rateLeadFrames` ahead, for ramps and held spans alike.
31	  - SR-14: the fourth spike's rule: the lead swept first on RK1 and RK2, then judged on a held-out RK3 and a gliding fixture.
32	  - SR-15: SR-13's arm lands at 56 ms though SR-14's run stopped; a deep slow-down plays up to about 22 ms late.
33	  - SR-16: SR1e closes as measured: the 56 ms lead stays, no closed loop and no re-fit; SR-15's limit widened.
34	  - SR-17: a corrected playback tap is trimmed, never zero-padded; a click outside it is unobserved.
35	  - SR-18: edits on a ramped clip through S: S∞ past the end, the head at the base rate, a split's halves meeting at S(cut).
36	  - SR-19: `set_speed` and `rate_stretch` scale the whole profile by one factor; copies and re-snaps carry a ramp; the ×12 figure is the greatest rate a clip names.
37	  - SR-20: `rc_project_source_map`, read only for a ramped clip through one interpolation; Synchronize Audio refuses a ramp.
38	  - SR-21: the UI: Rate inside a selected action writes its `end.speed`, the band names `speed`, the ×12 question for an end rate, the Speed sheet's ramp line, RMP-1..RMP-4.
39	  - SR-22: `set_action` refuses only an edit that takes an action further past its clip's end (#338).
40	  - Amended: SR-6 (by SR2a's two lines, SR2b's, SR-8 and SR-13); SR-7's PT1 (by SR-17); SR-8 (superseded by SR-13); SR-10 (by SR-18 and SR-19, twice); SR-11 (lifted by SR-13 and SR-15); SR-12 (i) (by SR-15); SR-15 (by SR-16); SR-18 (e) and (h) (by SR-19); SR-19 (i) (by SR-22); CI-6 (by SR-21).
41	
42	## Context
43	
44	#111 asked that a clip's rate can ramp from one value to another over a span, with playback and export agreeing frame for frame and sample for sample (a proof comparing export to expectation, made to fail on purpose once), undo working, and spec §5.2 and §6 describing it. A clip played at one rate (`Clip.speed`, `set_speed`, Clip ▸ Speed…), and AVFoundation's `scaleTimeRange` is piecewise-constant, so a ramp built from it is many abutting constant-rate segments. On 2026-10-23 the owner chose three things: a ramp is a Speed action on the existing lane; the clip keeps its slot and an edit past the media's end is refused; and audio follows the clip's own Keep pitch, with the road map opening on a spike that stops for the owner if the segments click or misplace audio. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices")
45	
46	## Decisions
47	
48	- **A rate is an action target, and the clip keeps its slot (SR-1, SR-2, SR-10).** `speed` is a top-level number in an action's `end`, clamped to ×0.1–×1000, on media clips only. Its integral S is in closed form per curve, so every reader gets one exact answer. A ramp edit never changes `start` or `duration`; the out point is `in + S(duration)`, and an edit that passes the media's end is refused with the largest end rate that fits (S is affine in one action's end rate), or else the latest clip end. A clip whose actions name no `speed` plans byte for byte as before. (orig rules A–C; SR2a)
49	- **The segments click, so the audio is rendered (SR-5, SR-6, SR-7).** SR1 ran the plan a ramp would emit through the app's own builder, exporter and player. At G1, V1 clicked at 30 of 61 boundaries in export, V2 at 69 of 91 and V3 at 52 of 121, mostly a slope kink about 45 samples before each boundary, where each time-scaled segment's varispeed unit starts afresh. Placement spread 1.4 ms against SY-27's 0.5 ms. Frames were right everywhere. V1L ruled out GO-UNIFORM-LEAD. The owner chose "Render it ourselves". In SR1b, every rendered ramp and control with Keep pitch off placed at +0.000 ms median and 0.000 ms spread, with no click, no dropout and no wrong frame, and the export was the render (≤ 1.53e-5, the WAV's quantisation). (orig SR1, SR1b)
50	- **Keep pitch on took four mechanisms (SR-8, SR-11, SR-13, SR-15, SR-16).**
51	  - SR1b's time-pitch unit, driven by a moving rate, misplaced RK1 by up to 33.48 ms and RK2 by up to 49.36 ms, against ceilings of 17.60 and 19.14.
52	  - SR1c's resample, then pitch-shift (SR-8) fixed the timing (max 1.21 ms) but dropped out 17 times through RK1's ramp, about every 117 ms. The owner chose "SR2 now, fix after", and SR-11's tape glide inside a ramp shipped as the interim.
53	  - SR1d's diagnostic found the dropouts are the unit's own in pitch mode: one each time a gliding partial crosses an 11.7 Hz analysis bin (RK1's 17 crossings, 17 dropouts). No block size, flag, smoothness or K removed them. Rate mode with the rate read ahead had none. The sweep picked L* = 56 ms (RK1 8.06 ms, RK2 5.55 ms), but the held-out RK3 (×2 → ×0.5 ease in-out) read 22.10 ms against 19.14. The owner chose "Land it, then tighten" (SR-15).
54	  - SR1e measured a closed loop. The unit's consumed input does not fix where its output sits: a controller cost more than it fixed, and an oracle loop did not converge. A 50 ms re-fit passed every held-out shape (minimax 11.38 ms), but it sits 3 ms from a cliff (RK3 15.01 ms at 53, 22.10 at 56, 36.60 at 60). The owner chose "Keep 56 ms, close SR1e" (SR-16).
55	  - Every mechanism stayed Apple's algorithm (SY-41).
56	  (orig SR1b, SR1c, SR1d, SR1e)
57	- **The instruments trim a corrected tap (SR-17).** The ×1 playback tap read 21.000 ms early in one session and 86.333 ms in another, on the same package and through a probe built before SR2b's app changes, so it is host state (#335). At −86.333 ms, zero-padding read as a 0.05 s "dropout" on every rendered clip, RC-off-x1 with Keep pitch off included. The correction now trims, and selftest S22 replays that reading. (orig SR2b "The tap offset (#335) is host state", SR1d "What it shows", SR1e)
58	- **One file per plan ramp segment, wanted by owners (SR-12).** A render is keyed by everything that shapes it and is ready iff its file exists, so no second state has to follow the disk. Renders run on one serial queue, and a render no owner wants is dropped, so an edit storm costs at most the one render in flight. An export waits for its renders and never writes a silent ramp. Two defects were found and fixed in SR2b:
59	  - The first Release run hung: an `AVAssetTrack` does not retain its asset, and an optimised build ended `rampAssets` before `fill` read their tracks. `build` now holds them with `withExtendedLifetime`.
60	  - The review found that a cancelled render wanted again was never re-queued, so an export waited at "Preparing…" until it was cancelled.
61	  (orig SR2b "Found on the way", "The review's fix")
62	- **A split's halves meet at S(cut) (SR-18).** The design review showed that an `ease_out` split re-eased to the rate at the cut repeated 1/3 s of footage. So the head's end rate is solved in closed form, and the rate steps at the cut for `ease_out` and `ease_in_out`. The cheaper loss is a rate step, not a repeated or skipped frame. (orig SR3a)
63	- **One factor scales the whole profile; one ×12 figure (SR-19).** A rate edit on a ramped clip multiplies the base, every end rate and every speed span by f, so the shape and the window are kept. The review found doubles miss by an ULP (×49 asked ×1 gave 0.9999999999999999), so an unclamped f writes the clamped rate itself. The ×12 test reads the greatest rate the clip names, the figure `SpeedAudioDrop` already read, so no rate is computed in Swift (D2-1). (orig SR3b)
64	- **Swift reads the core's map, only for a ramp (SR-20).** One export answers a clip's map, and `SourceMap` is the one read-side interpolation. It is checked once at decode and binary-searched both ways, because a map holds a point every 600 ticks and the waveform reads it per pixel column. A constant clip reads exactly as before. Synchronize Audio refuses a ramped clip, since its drift line assumes one rate. (orig SR4)
65	- **The inspector's rule carries over (SR-21, SR-22).** A field inside an action writes that action's end (CI-2), so Rate inside the selected action writes `end.speed`, and the rate shown comes from `clip_state.speed`. Keep pitch and Fit to stay the clip's. `set_action` refusing every edit of an action already past its clip's end left no way to re-curve one, so it now refuses only a further overrun (#338). (orig SR5)
66

The dev-only launch default `-RCDevRampRenderHold <s>` (SR-12 (j)).

103	
104	- **Keep pitch after a deep slow-down plays late** (SR-15, widened by SR-16). RK3 (×2 → ×0.5 ease in-out) reads up to 22.10 ms against SR-7's 19.14 ms ceiling, and SR1e's held-out shapes at 56 ms read H7 22.47 ms and H8 23.90 ms. For ×4 → ×1 (H3), 44 of 70 clicks are found, so about 26 are unmeasured. A 0.5 s ×3 → ×0.5 slow-down (H5) drops out once, with a 150-cent window. Only L3's case is pinned. # Speed ramps: a clip's rate changing over time, as a Speed action (road map "speed-ramps")

- **Status:** Built and closed 2026-10-24, for #111. Each phase was one litecode pipeline with its own review, worked in `~/devel/framejob-ramps` on branch `speed-ramps` and merged into main alone after its gate (SR-4). Five of them were spikes, each judged by a rule fixed before its run:
  - SR1, the road map, SR-1…SR-5 and the segment spike: STOP (`ffcb4b5`)
  - SR1b, the rendered-audio spike (SR-6, SR-7): SPLIT, off GO, on STOP (`874ecc8`)
  - SR1c, Keep pitch as resample, then pitch-shift (SR-8, SR-9): STOP (`214aee8`)
  - SR2a, `speed` as an action target, the speed map and the plan (SR-10, SR-11; format 27) (`2ee4e34`)
  - SR2b, the render wired into playback and export (SR-12) (`a579f71`), after its toll, `CompositionBuilder+Orientation.swift` (`5042934`)
  - SR1d, Keep pitch through Apple's time-pitch in rate mode with a 56 ms lead (SR-13…SR-15): STOP, landed on the owner's answer (`242f104`)
  - SR1e, the closed loop measured and closed (SR-16, SR-17) (`e2e79b9`)
  - SR3a, trims, roll, slip, split, freeze and the handle on a ramped clip (SR-18) (`27bbe72`)
  - SR3b, rate edits scale the whole profile; copies and re-snaps carry a ramp (SR-19) (`d35c716`)
  - SR4, Swift's mappers (SR-20) (`6a1b7a9`), after its toll, `CoreValues.swift` and `ReelOpSchema.swift` (`0b4be0b`)
  - SR5, the UI and #338 (SR-21, SR-22) (`6d1a968`), after its toll, `InspectorLabels.swift` (`a572d3f`)
  - The close: this record (the commit that moved the original to `archive/`)
- **Original:** `archive/speed-ramps.md` is the full record. It has no section numbers, so it is cited by its own headings: "orig SR2b" is its "SR2b — the renderer wired in" section, and "orig rule I" is the rule I bullet of its "Decided here".
- **Spec decisions:** SR-1..SR-22 in spec §11: SR-1…SR-12 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/speed-ramps.md`, SR-13…SR-22 in `speed-ramps-2.md` (split at the close by the spec's ~500-line rule). They stay binding, and where the original words them differently, §11's text wins:
  - SR-1: a speed ramp is a Speed action on the action lane, ramping from the rate in force to its end rate along its curve and held after.
  - SR-2: the clip keeps its slot; a ramp changes how much source it plays, and an edit reading past the media's end is refused, naming the rate or end that fits.
  - SR-3: audio follows the clip's own Keep pitch, with no time-stretch of Frame Job's own (SY-41).
  - SR-4: the working arrangement: the worktree, each phase gated and merged alone, synthetic fixtures, no `--live` run, owner media never read.
  - SR-5: the segment spike's rule: abutting constant-rate segments every G frames, judged for placement, click, dropout, video and agreement, and a verdict of GO, GO-UNIFORM-LEAD, GO-EXPORT-ONLY or STOP.
  - SR-6: a ramped clip's audio is rendered offline into `cache/ramp-audio/` and carried as one ×1 segment; with Keep pitch off, a Kaiser-windowed-sinc tape glide.
  - SR-7: the rendered-audio spike's rule: placement against the ideal map, a dense click scan, PT1's ×1 tap correction and a verdict per Keep pitch arm.
  - SR-8: Keep pitch on as resample, then pitch-shift (superseded whole by SR-13).
  - SR-9: the third spike's rule: SR-7's arm ON plus the rendered pitch and its lag.
  - SR-10: `end.speed`, the rate rule, S in closed form, per-frame video segments placed as one unit, one audio segment carrying the map, the slot's refusals and format 27.
  - SR-11: Keep pitch inside a ramp glided like tape as an interim (lifted by SR-13 and SR-15).
  - SR-12: the render wired in: a file per plan ramp segment, ready iff it exists, owners and one serial queue, the landing under the cache ledger, the export's wait.
  - SR-13: Keep pitch on is `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` in rate mode, its rate commanded `rateLeadFrames` ahead, for ramps and held spans alike.
  - SR-14: the fourth spike's rule: the lead swept first on RK1 and RK2, then judged on a held-out RK3 and a gliding fixture.
  - SR-15: SR-13's arm lands at 56 ms though SR-14's run stopped; a deep slow-down plays up to about 22 ms late.
  - SR-16: SR1e closes as measured: the 56 ms lead stays, no closed loop and no re-fit; SR-15's limit widened.
  - SR-17: a corrected playback tap is trimmed, never zero-padded; a click outside it is unobserved.
  - SR-18: edits on a ramped clip through S: S∞ past the end, the head at the base rate, a split's halves meeting at S(cut).
  - SR-19: `set_speed` and `rate_stretch` scale the whole profile by one factor; copies and re-snaps carry a ramp; the ×12 figure is the greatest rate a clip names.
  - SR-20: `rc_project_source_map`, read only for a ramped clip through one interpolation; Synchronize Audio refuses a ramp.
  - SR-21: the UI: Rate inside a selected action writes its `end.speed`, the band names `speed`, the ×12 question for an end rate, the Speed sheet's ramp line, RMP-1..RMP-4.
  - SR-22: `set_action` refuses only an edit that takes an action further past its clip's end (#338).
  - Amended: SR-6 (by SR2a's two lines, SR2b's, SR-8 and SR-13); SR-7's PT1 (by SR-17); SR-8 (superseded by SR-13); SR-10 (by SR-18 and SR-19, twice); SR-11 (lifted by SR-13 and SR-15); SR-12 (i) (by SR-15); SR-15 (by SR-16); SR-18 (e) and (h) (by SR-19); SR-19 (i) (by SR-22); CI-6 (by SR-21).

## Context

#111 asked that a clip's rate can ramp from one value to another over a span, with playback and export agreeing frame for frame and sample for sample (a proof comparing export to expectation, made to fail on purpose once), undo working, and spec §5.2 and §6 describing it. A clip played at one rate (`Clip.speed`, `set_speed`, Clip ▸ Speed…), and AVFoundation's `scaleTimeRange` is piecewise-constant, so a ramp built from it is many abutting constant-rate segments. On 2026-10-23 the owner chose three things: a ramp is a Speed action on the existing lane; the clip keeps its slot and an edit past the media's end is refused; and audio follows the clip's own Keep pitch, with the road map opening on a spike that stops for the owner if the segments click or misplace audio. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices")

## Decisions

- **A rate is an action target, and the clip keeps its slot (SR-1, SR-2, SR-10).** `speed` is a top-level number in an action's `end`, clamped to ×0.1–×1000, on media clips only. Its integral S is in closed form per curve, so every reader gets one exact answer. A ramp edit never changes `start` or `duration`; the out point is `in + S(duration)`, and an edit that passes the media's end is refused with the largest end rate that fits (S is affine in one action's end rate), or else the latest clip end. A clip whose actions name no `speed` plans byte for byte as before. (orig rules A–C; SR2a)
- **The segments click, so the audio is rendered (SR-5, SR-6, SR-7).** SR1 ran the plan a ramp would emit through the app's own builder, exporter and player. At G1, V1 clicked at 30 of 61 boundaries in export, V2 at 69 of 91 and V3 at 52 of 121, mostly a slope kink about 45 samples before each boundary, where each time-scaled segment's varispeed unit starts afresh. Placement spread 1.4 ms against SY-27's 0.5 ms. Frames were right everywhere. V1L ruled out GO-UNIFORM-LEAD. The owner chose "Render it ourselves". In SR1b, every rendered ramp and control with Keep pitch off placed at +0.000 ms median and 0.000 ms spread, with no click, no dropout and no wrong frame, and the export was the render (≤ 1.53e-5, the WAV's quantisation). (orig SR1, SR1b)
- **Keep pitch on took four mechanisms (SR-8, SR-11, SR-13, SR-15, SR-16).**
  - SR1b's time-pitch unit, driven by a moving rate, misplaced RK1 by up to 33.48 ms and RK2 by up to 49.36 ms, against ceilings of 17.60 and 19.14.
  - SR1c's resample, then pitch-shift (SR-8) fixed the timing (max 1.21 ms) but dropped out 17 times through RK1's ramp, about every 117 ms. The owner chose "SR2 now, fix after", and SR-11's tape glide inside a ramp shipped as the interim.
  - SR1d's diagnostic found the dropouts are the unit's own in pitch mode: one each time a gliding partial crosses an 11.7 Hz analysis bin (RK1's 17 crossings, 17 dropouts). No block size, flag, smoothness or K removed them. Rate mode with the rate read ahead had none. The sweep picked L* = 56 ms (RK1 8.06 ms, RK2 5.55 ms), but the held-out RK3 (×2 → ×0.5 ease in-out) read 22.10 ms against 19.14. The owner chose "Land it, then tighten" (SR-15).
  - SR1e measured a closed loop. The unit's consumed input does not fix where its output sits: a controller cost more than it fixed, and an oracle loop did not converge. A 50 ms re-fit passed every held-out shape (minimax 11.38 ms), but it sits 3 ms from a cliff (RK3 15.01 ms at 53, 22.10 at 56, 36.60 at 60). The owner chose "Keep 56 ms, close SR1e" (SR-16).
  - Every mechanism stayed Apple's algorithm (SY-41).
  (orig SR1b, SR1c, SR1d, SR1e)
- **The instruments trim a corrected tap (SR-17).** The ×1 playback tap read 21.000 ms early in one session and 86.333 ms in another, on the same package and through a probe built before SR2b's app changes, so it is host state (#335). At −86.333 ms, zero-padding read as a 0.05 s "dropout" on every rendered clip, RC-off-x1 with Keep pitch off included. The correction now trims, and selftest S22 replays that reading. (orig SR2b "The tap offset (#335) is host state", SR1d "What it shows", SR1e)
- **One file per plan ramp segment, wanted by owners (SR-12).** A render is keyed by everything that shapes it and is ready iff its file exists, so no second state has to follow the disk. Renders run on one serial queue, and a render no owner wants is dropped, so an edit storm costs at most the one render in flight. An export waits for its renders and never writes a silent ramp. Two defects were found and fixed in SR2b:
  - The first Release run hung: an `AVAssetTrack` does not retain its asset, and an optimised build ended `rampAssets` before `fill` read their tracks. `build` now holds them with `withExtendedLifetime`.
  - The review found that a cancelled render wanted again was never re-queued, so an export waited at "Preparing…" until it was cancelled.
  (orig SR2b "Found on the way", "The review's fix")
- **A split's halves meet at S(cut) (SR-18).** The design review showed that an `ease_out` split re-eased to the rate at the cut repeated 1/3 s of footage. So the head's end rate is solved in closed form, and the rate steps at the cut for `ease_out` and `ease_in_out`. The cheaper loss is a rate step, not a repeated or skipped frame. (orig SR3a)
- **One factor scales the whole profile; one ×12 figure (SR-19).** A rate edit on a ramped clip multiplies the base, every end rate and every speed span by f, so the shape and the window are kept. The review found doubles miss by an ULP (×49 asked ×1 gave 0.9999999999999999), so an unclamped f writes the clamped rate itself. The ×12 test reads the greatest rate the clip names, the figure `SpeedAudioDrop` already read, so no rate is computed in Swift (D2-1). (orig SR3b)
- **Swift reads the core's map, only for a ramp (SR-20).** One export answers a clip's map, and `SourceMap` is the one read-side interpolation. It is checked once at decode and binary-searched both ways, because a map holds a point every 600 ticks and the waveform reads it per pixel column. A constant clip reads exactly as before. Synchronize Audio refuses a ramped clip, since its drift line assumes one rate. (orig SR4)
- **The inspector's rule carries over (SR-21, SR-22).** A field inside an action writes that action's end (CI-2), so Rate inside the selected action writes `end.speed`, and the rate shown comes from `clip_state.speed`. Keep pitch and Fit to stay the clip's. `set_action` refusing every edit of an action already past its clip's end left no way to re-curve one, so it now refuses only a further overrun (#338). (orig SR5)

## What it built — where it lives now

- Rust, new: `speed_map.rs` (`SpeedMap`, `end_speed`, `is_ramped`, `ease_integral`, `of_length`, `time_for_source`, `head_end_rate`, `rate_at`, `rate_in_force`, `peak_rate`; SR2a, SR3a, SR3b, SR5), `speed_segments.rs` (`ramp_spans`, `ramp_audio`, `Project::source_map`; SR2a, SR4), `edit_action_speed.rs` (`read_speed_end`, R1–R3, `largest_fitting_end_rate`; SR2a, SR3a).
- Rust, changed: `evaluate.rs` (`Segment.ramp`, one clip's segments placed as one unit, the ×12 test on `peak_rate`), `source_window.rs` (the ramp arms of every bound, `source_read_by`, `source_advanced_through`, `front_edge_held`, `window_of`/`overrun`), `edit_action.rs` (the refusals wired in; SR-22's past-end test), `edit_clip_timing.rs` (`scaled_span`, `profile_factors`, `scaled_profile`), `frame_grid.rs` (`resnap_actions`, the second hold), the splitters, trims, roll and freeze, `actions.rs` (`clip_state`'s `speed`), `ffi_query.rs` (`rc_project_source_map`), the header; format 27.
- Rust tests: `ramp_plan.rs` (11), `ramp_door.rs` (9), `schema_v27.rs` (4), `ramp_trim.rs` (8), `ramp_split.rs` (10), `ramp_freeze.rs` (1), `ramp_transition.rs` (2), `ramp_reversed.rs` (2), `ramp_nest.rs` (2), `ramp_scale.rs` (12), `ramp_carry.rs` (10), `ramp_source_map.rs` (5), `ramp_inspector.rs` (8), each against closed-form oracles written in the file.
- Swift, new: `RampAudioRenderer.swift`, `RampAudioResampler.swift`, `RampCAFWriter.swift` and `RampAudioRenderer+TimePitch.swift` (SR1b; the last rewritten by SR1c, then by SR1d as SR-13's led rate-mode arm with `rateLeadFrames` 2 688), `RampVarispeedStream.swift` (SR1c, the Keep pitch off glide as a stream), `RampAudioCache.swift`, `RampAudioRenders.swift`, `ProjectDocument+RampAudio.swift` and `Exporter+RampAudio.swift` (SR2b), `SourceMap.swift` and `TimelineView+SourceMap.swift` (SR4). `RampAudioRenderer+Hybrid.swift` (SR2b, SR-11's mix) was deleted by SR1d.

## Known limits

- **Keep pitch after a deep slow-down plays late** (SR-15, widened by SR-16). - **The lead rests on Apple's unpublished behaviour** (SR-13): a macOS change to the time-pitch unit's window could move it. L1–L3 fail on Release when it does. Keep pitch on is measured against controls, never claimed sample-exact (SR-3).
- **A render after every map edit** (SR-12): the whole clip is rendered again, one render at a time (no partial re-render), and an undone map's file is not kept. A failure stays failed until relaunch. A ramp is silent until its render lands, and an export waits for it.
- **Many video segments** (SR-10): inside a ramp, one per canvas frame (30 a second at 30 fps).
- **Splits and trims** (SR-18): an `ease_out` or `ease_in_out` split steps the rate at the cut. An `ease_in` or `ease_in_out` split moves the second half's out point. A `trim_start` that would read past the file lands nearer its old start than asked.
- **Scaling and carries** (SR-19):
  - A clamped factor leaves the base off the asked rate.
  - A ramped `rate_stretch` that the hold trims lands up to a frame short.
  - A re-snap moves a ramp's out point by the grid's rounding.
  - A speed action can lie past its clip's end after any of these ops.
- **The named peak** (SR-19, SR-21): an end rate above ×12 on an action past the clip's end leaves the audio out and asks the ×12 question, though the clip never plays above ×12.
- **The slot's refusal** (SR-2): a fast ramp near the media's end is refused, not shortened.
- **Words and silences through the chord** (SR-20): they are placed through S's piecewise-linear chord, the one the renderer plays. Captions made before a ramp edit keep their old times until they are made again (rule O).
- **Synchronize Audio refuses a ramped clip** (SR-20 (e)), as mover or anchor.
- **`glide` shapes nothing** (SR-13): the core still writes it and the cache key still names it.
- **Synthetic fixtures only** (SR-4, SR-5): a click train, one sine and one sweep. A real voice and a real picture are the person's checks RMP-1..RMP-4 (SR-20 (h), SR-21 (h)).
- **Older defects the road map found, filed and outside it:**
  - #334: a constant ×4 clip's exported audio has sample steps (3 in SR1, 28 events in SR1b's dense scan; its rendered twin none). `retimed_audio_proof.py` B2 found them in AVFoundation's own read of the mix with no writer, about 0.17 s apart and at different times on each read, under the 16-bit read, the float read and an output-level varispeed alike. Frame Job's writer cannot fix it. The owner's question is whether to render constant Keep pitch off segments offline or to accept the limit.
  - #335: the ×1 playback tap reads 21.000 or 86.333 ms early, by host session; the instruments trim it (SR-17). Answered by spec §11 #335: on a track holding a ×1 clip alone, the PostEffects tap stamps its samples one 4,096-frame buffer early (−85.333 ms, 3 runs). The PreEffects tap, which is the product `AudioTap`'s flag, reads +0.000 ms, as does the export. Preview audio is in sync, and no product code changed.
  - #336: an export may fail when an audio track's only clip is all empty time (SR2b's PM2).
  - #337: a time-scaled clip's exported audio overruns or falls short of the timeline, run to run. CX2's `prores_422` audio was 196 095 frames in one run on a 4 s (192 000-frame) timeline, and CK05's was 1 213 frames (≈ 25 ms) short. U1 compares over the common length. Fixed by spec §11 #337: every export's audio is now exactly round(range × 48 000) frames, cut at the end and padded with silence (`ExportAudioEnd`; `retimed_audio_proof.py` A1–A3).

21	## Context
22	
23	Before this road map Frame Job exported H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. The owner's brief (2026-10-27) asked for AV1 and VP9 with the encoders bundled, and fixed four rows (AV1 in MP4 with AAC, AV1 in WebM with Opus, VP9 in WebM with Opus, VP9 with alpha in WebM; VP9 in MP4 not wanted), SVT-AV1 at three speeds (Faster 8, Balanced 6, Smaller file 4), libvpx at one, and a Rust WebM writer in the core rather than libwebm. The rest were the orchestrator's defaults, each the owner's to change: AudioToolbox's Opus, AV1 HDR first and VP9 Profile 2 later, pinned tarballs with no vendored source, the bitrate semantics kept, the M1/M2 decode gap documented, the encoders platform-side. Standing owner rules applied throughout: only higher-quality exports matter, memory limits relative to physical RAM, no feature size budget, person-only checks in `docs/manual-checks.md`. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices", "The orchestrator's defaults", "How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)")

25	## Decisions
26	
27	- **SVT-AV1, not libaom (CX-2, the spike).** At matched quality SVT-AV1 preset 4 equalled libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF over HEVC +3.36 against +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 against +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`) at about 41 fps against 13.6–16, about 3× faster; at matched speed SVT 8 gave +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37. libaom's best (good-3/4) is about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. libaom's favour: a higher worst frame (92 against 88) and half the memory. Presets 10 and 12 came within 0.7 VMAF of HEVC: no row. (orig S §2)
28	- **VP9 is for the web and alpha, not efficiency (CX-3).** libvpx good-4 needs 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality, but 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's; good-2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 % more time, rt-8 only HEVC's quality. (orig S §2)
29	- **The encoders are static, platform-side, built by `make codecs` (CX-4, CX-5).** No nasm, yasm, meson or ninja is needed on arm64 (Neon C intrinsics); cmake from Homebrew and the system perl are. The cold build is about 30 s; the stamp makes a warm one a no-op. Linked and stripped, SVT-AV1 adds 3.33 MB and libvpx 1.59 MB. `libSvtAv1Enc.a` carries `vector.c` (MIT), whose notice ships only through #376's acknowledgements (PUB-10). (orig S §1, C0)
30	- **The WebM writer is the core's (CX-6, CX-15).** Container bytes are decisions (timestamps, clusters, cues, CodecDelay), not sample work, as #216-R drew the line; the spike's libwebm files read back through the core's reader, which is the round-trip the core's tests now make against the writer. It is a second `ExportPipeline`, the one exception to §7.8's one writer, sharing the reader outputs, the pump, the gain, #337's end, the chapter partition, the size and the rates. (orig S §3, C3)
31	- **AV1 in MP4 goes through a passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (CX-12).** `canAdd` answered true for `av01`, and every frame decoded md5-identical. The core builds `av1C` from a full parse of the sequence header OBU, strips temporal delimiters and patches the `ftyp` to carry `av01`, which AV1-ISOBMFF requires and `AVAssetWriter` does not write (`rc_av1_*`). The writer reads sync samples from the bitstream itself: both `all-sync` and `no-sync` survived, so the attachment code went and A5's key-flag match is the guard. (orig S §3, C1, C1 fix pass)
32	- **AV1's rate is a soft cap, quality first (CX-13; the owner chose option 2, 2026-10-28).** Single-pass VBR (CX-9) undershot a real clip to 0.667–0.670 of its target. Every WebM stop is logged (`export.webm`), the Opus FIFO is fed by bytes, and the sound is placed at its stamps (`ExportAudioEnd.align`), not by count. (orig C3, C3 fix pass)
35	- **VP9's depth is the picture's, and the WebM Colour is its only transfer label (CX-16).** `sdr` is Profile 0 8-bit I420 BT.709; `hlg`/`pq` are Profile 2 10-bit I010 BT.2020. libvpx's bitstream carries a colour space but no transfer, so HLG and PQ live only in the container. (orig S §7, C4)

# Codec export: AV1 and VP9 through bundled SVT-AV1 and libvpx, in MP4 and WebM (road map "codec-export", #377)

- **Status:** Built and closed 2026-10-29, from the owner's brief of 2026-10-27 (#377: "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."). Each phase was one litecode pipeline with its own review, worked in `~/devel/framejob-codecs` on branch `codecs` (from `75fd806`), and gated, committed and merged into main alone (CX-11). A spike ran before C0 and committed nothing; C5 was rebased onto C6a, so C6a landed first:
  - S, the spike: encoders, containers, alpha, audio, the frame path and HDR measured; no product code
  - C0, CX-1..CX-11 and the encoder build: `make codecs`, SVT-AV1 and libvpx linked into every app (`61a2acc`)
  - C1, AV1 in MP4 at 8 bits, the Speed popup, capped constant quality (CX-12, CX-13) (`3e80381`)
  - C2, AV1 always 10-bit, with HLG, PQ and HDR10 (CX-14) (`5228645`)
  - C3, AV1 in WebM with Opus, through the core's WebM writer (CX-15) (`e759112`)
  - Release items between phases: the acknowledgements (#376), the encoders checked in the published app, the codecs cached in the publish workflow (PUB-10..PUB-12) (`ef3414f`); and #378, one `AVAssetReader` per output in `ExportWriter` (`d0f9fe0`)
  - C4, VP9 in WebM, 8-bit and Profile 2 HDR, and SDR WebM imports labelled (CX-16) (`546df3f`)
  - C6a, the encoder memory limit and the sheet's estimate (CX-18) (`998f0db`)
  - C5, VP9 with alpha in WebM (CX-17) (`cbf6e83`)
  - C6b, 4K on every row and the idle speed figures (CX-18 amended) (`4e01d24`)
  - The close: this record (the commit that moved the original to `archive/`)
- **Original:** `archive/codec-export.md` is the full record. It has no section numbers, so it is cited by its own headings: "orig C3" is its "C3 — AV1 in WebM, with Opus" section, "orig C1 fix pass" that phase's "Fix pass 1", and "orig S §3" the spike's "3. Containers".
- **Spec decisions:** CX-1..CX-18 in spec §11 (`designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`). They stay binding, and where the original or this record words them differently, §11's text wins:
  - CX-1 the four rows (owner); CX-2 SVT-AV1 alone and its three speeds (owner); CX-3 libvpx at one speed (owner); CX-4 the encoders platform-side; CX-5 the build policy; CX-6 the WebM writer in Rust (owner); CX-7 Opus from AudioToolbox; CX-8 HDR; CX-9 the rate model; CX-10 AV1 on M1/M2; CX-11 the working arrangement.
  - CX-12 C1's shape; CX-13 AV1's rate a soft cap, quality first (owner); CX-14 C2's one 10-bit `av1` row; CX-15 C3's `av1_webm`, writer and Opus; CX-16 C4's `vp9_webm` and the SDR import labels; CX-17 C5's `vp9_alpha_webm`; CX-18 C6a's memory limit and estimate, amended by C6b.
  - Amended: CX-5 (by PUB-10); CX-6 and CX-7 (by CX-15); CX-8 (by CX-16); CX-9 (1) and (4) on the AV1 rows (by CX-13); CX-12 (by CX-14, then CX-15); CX-13 (by CX-14); CX-14 (by CX-15); CX-15 (by CX-16, then CX-17); CX-16 (by CX-17); CX-17 (6) (in C5's fix pass, before its code); CX-18 (by C6b). This road map amended HD-5's row list, HD-14 (c), HD-18 (b), HD-19 (b), G-35 and #326's `queued` answer; #378's own §11 entry amends G-17.

## Context

Before this road map Frame Job exported H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. The owner's brief (2026-10-27) asked for AV1 and VP9 with the encoders bundled, and fixed four rows (AV1 in MP4 with AAC, AV1 in WebM with Opus, VP9 in WebM with Opus, VP9 with alpha in WebM; VP9 in MP4 not wanted), SVT-AV1 at three speeds (Faster 8, Balanced 6, Smaller file 4), libvpx at one, and a Rust WebM writer in the core rather than libwebm. The rest were the orchestrator's defaults, each the owner's to change: AudioToolbox's Opus, AV1 HDR first and VP9 Profile 2 later, pinned tarballs with no vendored source, the bitrate semantics kept, the M1/M2 decode gap documented, the encoders platform-side. Standing owner rules applied throughout: only higher-quality exports matter, memory limits relative to physical RAM, no feature size budget, person-only checks in `docs/manual-checks.md`. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices", "The orchestrator's defaults", "How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)")

## Decisions

- **SVT-AV1, not libaom (CX-2, the spike).** At matched quality SVT-AV1 preset 4 equalled libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF over HEVC +3.36 against +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 against +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`) at about 41 fps against 13.6–16, about 3× faster; at matched speed SVT 8 gave +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37. libaom's best (good-3/4) is about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. libaom's favour: a higher worst frame (92 against 88) and half the memory. Presets 10 and 12 came within 0.7 VMAF of HEVC: no row. (orig S §2)
- **VP9 is for the web and alpha, not efficiency (CX-3).** libvpx good-4 needs 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality, but 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's; good-2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 % more time, rt-8 only HEVC's quality. (orig S §2)
- **The encoders are static, platform-side, built by `make codecs` (CX-4, CX-5).** No nasm, yasm, meson or ninja is needed on arm64 (Neon C intrinsics); cmake from Homebrew and the system perl are. The cold build is about 30 s; the stamp makes a warm one a no-op. Linked and stripped, SVT-AV1 adds 3.33 MB and libvpx 1.59 MB. `libSvtAv1Enc.a` carries `vector.c` (MIT), whose notice ships only through #376's acknowledgements (PUB-10). (orig S §1, C0)
- **The WebM writer is the core's (CX-6, CX-15).** Container bytes are decisions (timestamps, clusters, cues, CodecDelay), not sample work, as #216-R drew the line; the spike's libwebm files read back through the core's reader, which is the round-trip the core's tests now make against the writer. It is a second `ExportPipeline`, the one exception to §7.8's one writer, sharing the reader outputs, the pump, the gain, #337's end, the chapter partition, the size and the rates. (orig S §3, C3)
- **AV1 in MP4 goes through a passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (CX-12).** `canAdd` answered true for `av01`, and every frame decoded md5-identical. The core builds `av1C` from a full parse of the sequence header OBU, strips temporal delimiters and patches the `ftyp` to carry `av01`, which AV1-ISOBMFF requires and `AVAssetWriter` does not write (`rc_av1_*`). The writer reads sync samples from the bitstream itself: both `all-sync` and `no-sync` survived, so the attachment code went and A5's key-flag match is the guard. (orig S §3, C1, C1 fix pass)
- **AV1's rate is a soft cap, quality first (CX-13; the owner chose option 2, 2026-10-28).** Single-pass VBR (CX-9) undershot a real clip to 0.667–0.670 of its target. Capped CRF replaced it, calibrated so each tier matches or beats HEVC's VMAF at HEVC's rate on the spike's three clips and on the owner's 55 s 1080p clip through the app itself, because SvtAv1EncApp's command-line scores did not transfer (1.1 VMAF lower for SVT-AV1 at one CRF and 1.6 for HEVC on that clip). A strict cap (12 % overshoot) left Faster under HEVC at Format default (a plateau at 95.055–95.348 against 95.469), because SVT-AV1 budgets each window's keyframes and base layers under the cap; SVT's default 50 % overshoot met every comparator. (orig C1 fix pass)
- **`av1` is always 10-bit, an HDR row (CX-14).** AV1's Main profile decodes 8 and 10 bits alike and only higher-quality exports matter, so there is no `av1_10bit`. The CICP is written in both the sequence header and `colr`, HDR10 (HD-5's fixed values) in both SVT-AV1's metadata OBUs and `mdcv`/`clli`; ffprobe's MP4 colour comes from `colr`, so H2's `trace_headers` is what catches a mislabelled bitstream. The owner-clip half of the CRF table was re-calibrated against `hevc_10bit`, which scores above 8-bit `hevc` (96.075 against 95.469 at Format default); the spike half stands at 8 bits. (orig C2)
- **G-17 closed on the WebM path by one reader per output (CX-15 (2)).** C3 met one hang, a video pump blocked in `copyNextSampleBuffer` with the audio pump gone (#379). Cancelling a shared reader from the other thread is what G-17 measured crashing 12 of 30 cancels, so each pump now reads and cancels its own `AVAssetReader`; R1 measured the two-reader read equal frame for frame and sample for sample. #378 then did the same for `ExportWriter`. Every WebM stop is logged (`export.webm`), the Opus FIFO is fed by bytes, and the sound is placed at its stamps (`ExportAudioEnd.align`), not by count. (orig C3, C3 fix pass)
- **VP9's depth is the picture's, and the WebM Colour is its only transfer label (CX-16).** `sdr` is Profile 0 8-bit I420 BT.709; `hlg`/`pq` are Profile 2 10-bit I010 BT.2020. libvpx's bitstream carries a colour space but no transfer, so HLG and PQ live only in the container. (orig S §7, C4)
- **An SDR WebM copy is labelled from its source (CX-16 (10), RULING-1).** V10 re-imported Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` with cyan coming back (23, 255, 255): BT.709 decoded as BT.601, because the rewrap's copy carried no colour and AVFoundation chose the matrix by size. The copy now carries the Colour's codes, else a VP9 keyframe's `color_space` for the matrix (`stream_matrix`); V10 then read 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96 of 255. (orig C4 "RULING-1")
- **VP9 alpha is a second encoder (CX-17).** libvpx has no alpha input; the alpha plane is a second 8-bit picture (Y = round(255·a), full range, chroma 128) at constant quality, keys forced on the same frames, packets paired by pts, written as BlockAdditional 1 with `AlphaMode` 1 and a ReferenceBlock on non-keys. AV1 alpha does not exist in practice (no API input, no Matroska mapping). The frames are straightened first (G-35). The alpha level is banded by size so every band holds 48 dB at its worst frame (C5 fix pass, RULING-1). (orig S §4, C5, C5 fix pass)
- **The memory limit is a ledger, not a pool (CX-18).** The queue stays one job at a time; a bundled-encoder job is held while the app's running encoder exports (the queue's and every Export… sheet's) and it would pass a quarter of physical memory, each costed by its measured peak per key, scaled by pixels. A sheet is counted, never held; a held job is passed over and says why. On a 32 GiB Mac that admits one AV1 job at 4K at any speed; on 16 GiB one AV1 4K job always runs alone. (orig C6a)
- **The estimate is fitted on real footage (CX-18 amended by C6b).** C6a's single-run constants, on AV.mov scaled up, were 50–79 % short of real footage. C6b took idle three-run medians on the GH5 4K clip, fitting a fixed start from a 250-frame and a 50-frame batch; `av1_webm` copies `av1`'s times (within 10 %). (orig C6a, C6b)

## Known limits

- **AV1 cannot be decoded on an M1 or M2** (CX-10): the export works, but Frame Job cannot preview or re-import its own AV1 file there, and the proofs read AV1 through ffmpeg; playback is SE-17 and SE-18 on an M3 or later.
- **A soft cap, not a ceiling** (CX-13, CX-16 (7)): a file usually stays under its rate but can pass it, measured up to 1.254 × on AV1 and 1.143 × on VP9; the guide says about 1.25 × and 1.15 ×. The calibration is four clips at 1080p, one of them binding, and other sizes are placed by bits per pixel alone.
- **Faster at Maximum sits 0.059 VMAF under `hevc_10bit`** (CX-14 (6), the owner's "Best CRF, accept 0.06"): below CRF 12 the cap binds and a lower CRF gains nothing.
- **Thin margins against a moving comparator**: VideoToolbox's `hevc` and `hevc_10bit` read a few hundredths differently run to run (95.338 and 95.469; one 10-bit encode 0.25 lower under load), and VP9's 8-bit Medium (+0.016) and Format default (+0.029) cells are kept by that much.
- **The spike half of AV1's calibration stands at 8 bits** (CX-14 (6)); only the owner-clip half was re-run against `hevc_10bit`.
- **A `vp9_alpha_webm` re-imports opaque** (CX-17 (7)): the rewrap copies the Block and not the BlockAdditional, and Apple's VP9 decoder has no alpha (#381). ffmpeg's native `vp9` decoder ignores the alpha too; only libvpx's reads it. Safari's playback is SE-21's question.
- **No HDR or 10-bit alpha, no AV1 alpha, no VP9 in MP4** (CX-1, CX-17 (8)).
- **One VP9 speed** (CX-3, CX-16 (2)): the Speed popup is disabled on the VP9 rows.
- **The HDR rendering is a person's** (HDR-8): ffmpeg's Matroska demuxer exports no content-light-level side data when MaxFALL is 0, which HD-5's fixed values make it, though the walk reads MaxCLL 1000 / MaxFALL 0 in the Colour.
- **Opus undershoots its rate**: AudioToolbox at 192 kb/s wrote about 119 kb/s on A1's sound (CX-7).
- **The cost tables are one machine and one picture** (CX-18): a heavier timeline or harder footage can exceed a peak or take longer, and a sheet export can take the app past the budget (CX-18 (6)). VP9's estimate runs 12–14 % high at 1440p, its per-frame time growing slower than the pixels between the two measured sizes; within the tolerance and not re-tuned.
- **GIF and APNG are outside the ledger**: a 4K GIF peaked 11.48 GiB and a 4K APNG 7.85 GiB above baseline (C6b's A), neither booked because neither is a writer row (#383).

## Open items

- #377, the brief: every phase built; closed by the close's commit.
- #376 (acknowledgements, `ef3414f`) and #378 (G-17 on `ExportWriter`, `d0f9fe0`): closed.
- #379: open. C3's one unreproduced hang, the WebM audio pump stopping early; one reader per output closed the starvation it caused, but its cause was not found in 42 later exports.
- #381: open. Keeping a `vp9_alpha_webm`'s alpha on re-import (C5's "to file").
- #382: open. An `av1` MP4 export hung once in `encoder_limit_proof.py`'s Q1, its video read stuck in `copyNextSampleBuffer` with no compositor request in flight (C5's fix pass).
- #383: open. 4K GIF and APNG memory outside the encoder limit (C6b's finding 2).
- #380: open, filed beside #376's acknowledgements: whether the LGPL-2 JavaScriptCore inside the bun-compiled assistant helper needs more than a notice. Not this road map's code.
- Nothing else is known to be unfinished, so no issue was filed at the close.

Not filed, each decided:
- C3's re-review nit: no app row shows `align`'s gap fill or head cut (E40 does not show whether the first buffer straddled the in point); `webm_audio_probe.swift`'s A1–A5 are its proof.
- VP9's 1440p over-estimate: within CX-18's 25 % tolerance, recorded above.
- `AgentCatalog+Render.swift` at 402 lines after C5's merge, past the 400 a new file starts under: its next text pays a toll first (the size rule).
- Every `rc_*` wrapper lands in `ReelCore.swift`, over the ~600 cap, so each new export pays a toll there: the standing rule in `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` ("Any addition to `ReelCore.swift` pays for itself first"), followed by C1, C3 and C5.
- C4's `export_gain_proof.py --against …/gain-before` was not run (no control on that host); H7i's first failure was a missing control capture, not the change (orig C4 fix pass).
- The `CLAUDE.md` edits each phase listed as owed are all in the per-side files and the root file.

## Where to look in the original

- "Goal", "The owner's choices" and "The orchestrator's defaults": the brief's binding rows and the defaults the owner may change.
- "How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)": the export table, writer, WebM reader, build and bridge the phases started from.
- "Phases": what each phase was to build, and its acceptance.
- "S — the spike": the instruments and test clips; §1 the pins, build commands, build times, link sizes and licences of libaom, SVT-AV1, libvpx, libopus and libwebm; §2 the VMAF, speed and RSS tables per encoder and preset, and the recommendation; §3 AV1 and VP9 in MP4 (`av1C`, TDs, the `ftyp` brand, no AV1 decode on M2) and libwebm against a core writer; §4 alpha and the browsers; §5 AudioToolbox's Opus; §6 the frame path's conversion costs, queue and memory; §7 HDR per codec and container; "Risks".
- "C0 — decisions and the encoder build": the pins' digests, the build's commands and outputs, D36–D41, `vector.c`.
- "C1 — AV1 in MP4": the tolls, the row, the VBR rate runs, the nine mutants and the equivalent `all-sync`/`open-gop`; its "Fix pass 1": the capped-CRF calibration (spike and through the app), the strict cap's failure, the four options put to the owner and Ruling 2.
- "C2 — AV1 at 10 bits, with HLG, PQ and HDR10": the 10-bit calibration, the outlier `hevc_10bit` encode, the Faster-at-Maximum ruling, H4's code values and the nine mutants.
- "C3 — AV1 in WebM, with Opus": the tolls, the writer's files, the eight mutants, ffmpeg's readings of key flags, CodecDelay and MaxFALL, the hang; its fix pass: one reader per output, F1–F3, the FIFO by bytes, `align`.

- "C5 — VP9 with alpha in WebM": the tolls, the alpha's calibration, the mutants; its "Fix pass 1": the rebase onto C6a, the alpha row's memory run, RULING-1's size bands and the `av1` hang.
- "C6a — the Export Queue's memory limit and the sheet's estimate": the first memory and time table, what the limit means per RAM size, Q1–Q5 and the ten mutants; its "Fix pass 1": the tooltip, `phase7_chrome.py`'s band and `graphic/tests/path.rs`'s CPU-time budget.

42	## Context
43	
44	#111 asked that a clip's rate can ramp from one value to another over a span, with playback and export agreeing frame for frame and sample for sample (a proof comparing export to expectation, made to fail on purpose once), undo working, and spec §5.2 and §6 describing it. A clip played at one rate (`Clip.speed`, `set_speed`, Clip ▸ Speed…), and AVFoundation's `scaleTimeRange` is piecewise-constant, so a ramp built from it is many abutting constant-rate segments. On 2026-10-23 the owner chose three things: a ramp is a Speed action on the existing lane; the clip keeps its slot and an edit past the media's end is refused; and audio follows the clip's own Keep pitch, with the road map opening on a spike that stops for the owner if the segments click or misplace audio. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices")
45	
46	## Decisions
47	
48	- **A rate is an action target, and the clip keeps its slot (SR-1, SR-2, SR-10).** `speed` is a top-level number in an action's `end`, clamped to ×0.1–×1000, on media clips only. Its integral S is in closed form per curve, so every reader gets one exact answer. A ramp edit never changes `start` or `duration`; the out point is `in + S(duration)`, and an edit that passes the media's end is refused with the largest end rate that fits (S is affine in one action's end rate), or else the latest clip end. A clip whose actions name no `speed` plans byte for byte as before. (orig rules A–C; SR2a)
49	- **The segments click, so the audio is rendered (SR-5, SR-6, SR-7).** SR1 ran the plan a ramp would emit through the app's own builder, exporter and player. At G1, V1 clicked at 30 of 61 boundaries in export, V2 at 69 of 91 and V3 at 52 of 121, mostly a slope kink about 45 samples before each boundary, where each time-scaled segment's varispeed unit starts afresh. Placement spread 1.4 ms against SY-27's 0.5 ms. Frames were right everywhere. V1L ruled out GO-UNIFORM-LEAD. The owner chose "Render it ourselves". In SR1b, every rendered ramp and control with Keep pitch off placed at +0.000 ms median and 0.000 ms spread, with no click, no dropout and no wrong frame, and the export was the render (≤ 1.53e-5, the WAV's quantisation). (orig SR1, SR1b)
50	- **Keep pitch on took four mechanisms (SR-8, SR-11, SR-13, SR-15, SR-16).**
51	  - SR1b's time-pitch unit, driven by a moving rate, misplaced RK1 by up to 33.48 ms and RK2 by up to 49.36 ms, against ceilings of 17.60 and 19.14.
52	  - SR1c's resample, then pitch-shift (SR-8) fixed the timing (max 1.21 ms) but dropped out 17 times through RK1's ramp, about every 117 ms. The owner chose "SR2 now, fix after", and SR-11's tape glide inside a ramp shipped as the interim.
53	  - SR1d's diagnostic found the dropouts are the unit's own in pitch mode: one each time a gliding partial crosses an 11.7 Hz analysis bin (RK1's 17 crossings, 17 dropouts). No block size, flag, smoothness or K removed them. Rate mode with the rate read ahead had none. The sweep picked L* = 56 ms (RK1 8.06 ms, RK2 5.55 ms), but the held-out RK3 (×2 → ×0.5 ease in-out) read 22.10 ms against 19.14. The owner chose "Land it, then tighten" (SR-15).
54	  - SR1e measured a closed loop. The unit's consumed input does not fix where its output sits: a controller cost more than it fixed, and an oracle loop did not converge. A 50 ms re-fit passed every held-out shape (minimax 11.38 ms), but it sits 3 ms from a cliff (RK3 15.01 ms at 53, 22.10 at 56, 36.60 at 60). The owner chose "Keep 56 ms, close SR1e" (SR-16).
55	  - Every mechanism stayed Apple's algorithm (SY-41).
56	  (orig SR1b, SR1c, SR1d, SR1e)
57	- **The instruments trim a corrected tap (SR-17).** The ×1 playback tap read 21.000 ms early in one session and 86.333 ms in another, on the same package and through a probe built before SR2b's app changes, so it is host state (#335). At −86.333 ms, zero-padding read as a 0.05 s "dropout" on every rendered clip, RC-off-x1 with Keep pitch off included. The correction now trims, and selftest S22 replays that reading. (orig SR2b "The tap offset (#335) is host state", SR1d "What it shows", SR1e)
58	- **One file per plan ramp segment, wanted by owners (SR-12).** A render is keyed by everything that shapes it and is ready iff its file exists, so no second state has to follow the disk. Renders run on one serial queue, and a render no owner wants is dropped, so an edit storm costs at most the one render in flight. An export waits for its renders and never writes a silent ramp. Two defects were found and fixed in SR2b:
59	  - The first Release run hung: an `AVAssetTrack` does not retain its asset, and an optimised build ended `rampAssets` before `fill` read their tracks. `build` now holds them with `withExtendedLifetime`.
60	  - The review found that a cancelled render wanted again was never re-queued, so an export waited at "Preparing…" until it was cancelled.
61	  (orig SR2b "Found on the way", "The review's fix")
62	- **A split's halves meet at S(cut) (SR-18).** The design review showed that an `ease_out` split re-eased to the rate at the cut repeated 1/3 s of footage. So the head's end rate is solved in closed form, and the rate steps at the cut for `ease_out` and `ease_in_out`. The cheaper loss is a rate step, not a repeated or skipped frame. (orig SR3a)
63	- **One factor scales the whole profile; one ×12 figure (SR-19).** A rate edit on a ramped clip multiplies the base, every end rate and every speed span by f, so the shape and the window are kept. The review found doubles miss by an ULP (×49 asked ×1 gave 0.9999999999999999), so an unclamped f writes the clamped rate itself. The ×12 test reads the greatest rate the clip names, the figure `SpeedAudioDrop` already read, so no rate is computed in Swift (D2-1). (orig SR3b)
64	- **Swift reads the core's map, only for a ramp (SR-20).** One export answers a clip's map, and `SourceMap` is the one read-side interpolation. It is checked once at decode and binary-searched both ways, because a map holds a point every 600 ticks and the waveform reads it per pixel column. A constant clip reads exactly as before. Synchronize Audio refuses a ramped clip, since its drift line assumes one rate. (orig SR4)
65	- **The inspector's rule carries over (SR-21, SR-22).** A field inside an action writes that action's end (CI-2), so Rate inside the selected action writes `end.speed`, and the rate shown comes from `clip_state.speed`. Keep pitch and Fit to stay the clip's. `set_action` refusing every edit of an action already past its clip's end left no way to re-curve one, so it now refuses only a further overrun (#338). (orig SR5)

102	## Known limits
103	
104	- **Keep pitch after a deep slow-down plays late** (SR-15, widened by SR-16). RK3 (×2 → ×0.5 ease in-out) reads up to 22.10 ms against SR-7's 19.14 ms ceiling, and SR1e's held-out shapes at 56 ms read H7 22.47 ms and H8 23.90 ms. For ×4 → ×1 (H3), 44 of 70 clicks are found, so about 26 are unmeasured. A 0.5 s ×3 → ×0.5 slow-down (H5) drops out once, with a 150-cent window. Only L3's case is pinned. The owner declined the 50 ms re-fit ("Keep 56 ms, close SR1e").
105	- **The lead rests on Apple's unpublished behaviour** (SR-13): a macOS change to the time-pitch unit's window could move it. L1–L3 fail on Release when it does. Keep pitch on is measured against controls, never claimed sample-exact (SR-3).
106	- **A render after every map edit** (SR-12): the whole clip is rendered again, one render at a time (no partial re-render), and an undone map's file is not kept. A failure stays failed until relaunch. A ramp is silent until its render lands, and an export waits for it.
107	- **Many video segments** (SR-10): inside a ramp, one per canvas frame (30 a second at 30 fps).
108	- **Splits and trims** (SR-18): an `ease_out` or `ease_in_out` split steps the rate at the cut. An `ease_in` or `ease_in_out` split moves the second half's out point. A `trim_start` that would read past the file lands nearer its old start than asked.
109	- **Scaling and carries** (SR-19):
110	  - A clamped factor leaves the base off the asked rate.
111	  - A ramped `rate_stretch` that the hold trims lands up to a frame short.
112	  - A re-snap moves a ramp's out point by the grid's rounding.
113	  - A speed action can lie past its clip's end after any of these ops.
114	- **The named peak** (SR-19, SR-21): an end rate above ×12 on an action past the clip's end leaves the audio out and asks the ×12 question, though the clip never plays above ×12.
115	- **The slot's refusal** (SR-2): a fast ramp near the media's end is refused, not shortened.
116	- **Words and silences through the chord** (SR-20): they are placed through S's piecewise-linear chord, the one the renderer plays. Captions made before a ramp edit keep their old times until they are made again (rule O).
117	- **Synchronize Audio refuses a ramped clip** (SR-20 (e)), as mover or anchor.
118	- **`glide` shapes nothing** (SR-13): the core still writes it and the cache key still names it.
119	- **Synthetic fixtures only** (SR-4, SR-5): a click train, one sine and one sweep. A real voice and a real picture are the person's checks RMP-1..RMP-4 (SR-20 (h), SR-21 (h)).
120	- **Older defects the road map found, filed and outside it:**
121	  - #334: a constant ×4 clip's exported audio has sample steps (3 in SR1, 28 events in SR1b's dense scan; its rendered twin none). `retimed_audio_proof.py` B2 found them in AVFoundation's own read of the mix with no writer, about 0.17 s apart and at different times on each read, under the 16-bit read, the float read and an output-level varispeed alike. Frame Job's writer cannot fix it. The owner's question is whether to render constant Keep pitch off segments offline or to accept the limit.
122	  - #335: the ×1 playback tap reads 21.000 or 86.333 ms early, by host session; the instruments trim it (SR-17). Answered by spec §11 #335: on a track holding a ×1 clip alone, the PostEffects tap stamps its samples one 4,096-frame buffer early (−85.333 ms, 3 runs). The PreEffects tap, which is the product `AudioTap`'s flag, reads +0.000 ms, as does the export. Preview audio is in sync, and no product code changed.

CX2's `prores_422` audio was 196 095 frames in one run on a 4 s (192 000-frame) timeline, and CK05's was 1 213 frames (≈ 25 ms) short. U1 compares over the common length. 21	## Context
22	
23	Before this road map Frame Job exported H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. The owner's brief (2026-10-27) asked for AV1 and VP9 with the encoders bundled, and fixed four rows (AV1 in MP4 with AAC, AV1 in WebM with Opus, VP9 in WebM with Opus, VP9 with alpha in WebM; VP9 in MP4 not wanted), SVT-AV1 at three speeds (Faster 8, Balanced 6, Smaller file 4), libvpx at one, and a Rust WebM writer in the core rather than libwebm. The rest were the orchestrator's defaults, each the owner's to change: AudioToolbox's Opus, AV1 HDR first and VP9 Profile 2 later, pinned tarballs with no vendored source, the bitrate semantics kept, the M1/M2 decode gap documented, the encoders platform-side. Standing owner rules applied throughout: only higher-quality exports matter, memory limits relative to physical RAM, no feature size budget, person-only checks in `docs/manual-checks.md`. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices", "The orchestrator's defaults", "How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)")

25	## Decisions
26	
27	- **SVT-AV1, not libaom (CX-2, the spike).** At matched quality SVT-AV1 preset 4 equalled libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF over HEVC +3.36 against +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 against +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`) at about 41 fps against 13.6–16, about 3× faster; at matched speed SVT 8 gave +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37. libaom's best (good-3/4) is about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. libaom's favour: a higher worst frame (92 against 88) and half the memory. Presets 10 and 12 came within 0.7 VMAF of HEVC: no row. (orig S §2)
28	- **VP9 is for the web and alpha, not efficiency (CX-3).** libvpx good-4 needs 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality, but 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's; good-2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 % more time, rt-8 only HEVC's quality. (orig S §2)
29	- **The encoders are static, platform-side, built by `make codecs` (CX-4, CX-5).** No nasm, yasm, meson or ninja is needed on arm64 (Neon C intrinsics); cmake from Homebrew and the system perl are. The cold build is about 30 s; the stamp makes a warm one a no-op. Linked and stripped, SVT-AV1 adds 3.33 MB and libvpx 1.59 MB. `libSvtAv1Enc.a` carries `vector.c` (MIT), whose notice ships only through #376's acknowledgements (PUB-10). (orig S §1, C0)
30	- **The WebM writer is the core's (CX-6, CX-15).** Container bytes are decisions (timestamps, clusters, cues, CodecDelay), not sample work, as #216-R drew the line; the spike's libwebm files read back through the core's reader, which is the round-trip the core's tests now make against the writer. It is a second `ExportPipeline`, the one exception to §7.8's one writer, sharing the reader outputs, the pump, the gain, #337's end, the chapter partition, the size and the rates. (orig S §3, C3)
31	- **AV1 in MP4 goes through a passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (CX-12).** `canAdd` answered true for `av01`, and every frame decoded md5-identical. The core builds `av1C` from a full parse of the sequence header OBU, strips temporal delimiters and patches the `ftyp` to carry `av01`, which AV1-ISOBMFF requires and `AVAssetWriter` does not write (`rc_av1_*`). The writer reads sync samples from the bitstream itself: both `all-sync` and `no-sync` survived, so the attachment code went and A5's key-flag match is the guard. (orig S §3, C1, C1 fix pass)
32	- **AV1's rate is a soft cap, quality first (CX-13; the owner chose option 2, 2026-10-28).** Single-pass VBR (CX-9) undershot a real clip to 0.667–0.670 of its target. Capped CRF replaced it, calibrated so each tier matches or beats HEVC's VMAF at HEVC's rate on the spike's three clips and on the owner's 55 s 1080p clip through the app itself, because SvtAv1EncApp's command-line scores did not transfer (1.1 VMAF lower for SVT-AV1 at one CRF and 1.6 for HEVC on that clip). A strict cap (12 % overshoot) left Faster under HEVC at Format default (a plateau at 95.055–95.348 against 95.469), because SVT-AV1 budgets each window's keyframes and base layers under the cap; SVT's default 50 % overshoot met every comparator. (orig C1 fix pass)
33	- **`av1` is always 10-bit, an HDR row (CX-14).** AV1's Main profile decodes 8 and 10 bits alike and only higher-quality exports matter, so there is no `av1_10bit`. The CICP is written in both the sequence header and `colr`, HDR10 (HD-5's fixed values) in both SVT-AV1's metadata OBUs and `mdcv`/`clli`; ffprobe's MP4 colour comes from `colr`, so H2's `trace_headers` is what catches a mislabelled bitstream. The owner-clip half of the CRF table was re-calibrated against `hevc_10bit`, which scores above 8-bit `hevc` (96.075 against 95.469 at Format default); the spike half stands at 8 bits. (orig C2)
34	- **G-17 closed on the WebM path by one reader per output (CX-15 (2)).** C3 met one hang, a video pump blocked in `copyNextSampleBuffer` with the audio pump gone (#379). Cancelling a shared reader from the other thread is what G-17 measured crashing 12 of 30 cancels, so each pump now reads and cancels its own `AVAssetReader`; R1 measured the two-reader read equal frame for frame and sample for sample. #378 then did the same for `ExportWriter`. Every WebM stop is logged (`export.webm`), the Opus FIFO is fed by bytes, and the sound is placed at its stamps (`ExportAudioEnd.align`), not by count. (orig C3, C3 fix pass)
35	- **VP9's depth is the picture's, and the WebM Colour is its only transfer label (CX-16).** `sdr` is Profile 0 8-bit I420 BT.709; `hlg`/`pq` are Profile 2 10-bit I010 BT.2020. libvpx's bitstream carries a colour space but no transfer, so HLG and PQ live only in the container. (orig S §7, C4)
36	- **An SDR WebM copy is labelled from its source (CX-16 (10), RULING-1).** V10 re-imported Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` with cyan coming back (23, 255, 255): BT.709 decoded as BT.601, because the rewrap's copy carried no colour and AVFoundation chose the matrix by size. The copy now carries the Colour's codes, else a VP9 keyframe's `color_space` for the matrix (`stream_matrix`); V10 then read 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96 of 255. (orig C4 "RULING-1")
37	- **VP9 alpha is a second encoder (CX-17).** libvpx has no alpha input; the alpha plane is a second 8-bit picture (Y = round(255·a), full range, chroma 128) at constant quality, keys forced on the same frames, packets paired by pts, written as BlockAdditional 1 with `AlphaMode` 1 and a ReferenceBlock on non-keys. AV1 alpha does not exist in practice (no API input, no Matroska mapping). The frames are straightened first (G-35). The alpha level is banded by size so every band holds 48 dB at its worst frame (C5 fix pass, RULING-1). (orig S §4, C5, C5 fix pass)
38	- **The memory limit is a ledger, not a pool (CX-18).** The queue stays one job at a time; a bundled-encoder job is held while the app's running encoder exports (the queue's and every Export… sheet's) and it would pass a quarter of physical memory, each costed by its measured peak per key, scaled by pixels. A sheet is counted, never held; a held job is passed over and says why. On a 32 GiB Mac that admits one AV1 job at 4K at any speed; on 16 GiB one AV1 4K job always runs alone. (orig C6a)
39	- **The estimate is fitted on real footage (CX-18 amended by C6b).** C6a's single-run constants, on AV.mov scaled up, were 50–79 % short of real footage. C6b took idle three-run medians on the GH5 4K clip, fitting a fixed start from a 250-frame and a 50-frame batch; `av1_webm` copies `av1`'s times (within 10 %). (orig C6a, C6b)

73	## Known limits
74	
75	- **AV1 cannot be decoded on an M1 or M2** (CX-10): the export works, but Frame Job cannot preview or re-import its own AV1 file there, and the proofs read AV1 through ffmpeg; playback is SE-17 and SE-18 on an M3 or later.
76	- **A soft cap, not a ceiling** (CX-13, CX-16 (7)): a file usually stays under its rate but can pass it, measured up to 1.254 × on AV1 and 1.143 × on VP9; the guide says about 1.25 × and 1.15 ×. The calibration is four clips at 1080p, one of them binding, and other sizes are placed by bits per pixel alone.
77	- **Faster at Maximum sits 0.059 VMAF under `hevc_10bit`** (CX-14 (6), the owner's "Best CRF, accept 0.06"): below CRF 12 the cap binds and a lower CRF gains nothing.
78	- **Thin margins against a moving comparator**: VideoToolbox's `hevc` and `hevc_10bit` read a few hundredths differently run to run (95.338 and 95.469; one 10-bit encode 0.25 lower under load), and VP9's 8-bit Medium (+0.016) and Format default (+0.029) cells are kept by that much.
79	- **The spike half of AV1's calibration stands at 8 bits** (CX-14 (6)); only the owner-clip half was re-run against `hevc_10bit`.
80	- **A `vp9_alpha_webm` re-imports opaque** (CX-17 (7)): the rewrap copies the Block and not the BlockAdditional, and Apple's VP9 decoder has no alpha (#381). ffmpeg's native `vp9` decoder ignores the alpha too; only libvpx's reads it. Safari's playback is SE-21's question.
81	- **No HDR or 10-bit alpha, no AV1 alpha, no VP9 in MP4** (CX-1, CX-17 (8)).
82	- **One VP9 speed** (CX-3, CX-16 (2)): the Speed popup is disabled on the VP9 rows.
83	- **The HDR rendering is a person's** (HDR-8): ffmpeg's Matroska demuxer exports no content-light-level side data when MaxFALL is 0, which HD-5's fixed values make it, though the walk reads MaxCLL 1000 / MaxFALL 0 in the Colour.
84	- **Opus undershoots its rate**: AudioToolbox at 192 kb/s wrote about 119 kb/s on A1's sound (CX-7).
85	- **The cost tables are one machine and one picture** (CX-18): a heavier timeline or harder footage can exceed a peak or take longer, and a sheet export can take the app past the budget (CX-18 (6)). VP9's estimate runs 12–14 % high at 1440p, its per-frame time growing slower than the pixels between the two measured sizes; within the tolerance and not re-tuned.
86	- **GIF and APNG are outside the ledger**: a 4K GIF peaked 11.48 GiB and a 4K APNG 7.85 GiB above baseline (C6b's A), neither booked because neither is a writer row (#383).

37	## Decisions
38	
39	- **The PQ peak is read by two routes, MaxCLL first.** AVFoundation reads a sample description's `mdcv`/`clli` but not the HEVC SEI, and files from ffmpeg, HandBrake or x265 carry the SEI only (M5). So import reads the description's two extensions first and, failing those, the first sample's prefix SEI 137/144, parsed from bytes by a pure core reader (`rc_hdr10_peak`). The peak is MaxCLL when present and non-zero, else the mastering maximum, clamped to 10,000; unknown means 1,000, so every unlabelled file is byte-identical. Apple's own conversion ignores the metadata either way. (orig "#281 — the PQ peak (H-1, HD-6; the brief's §3)", H-1; HD-6, HD-12)
40	- **An HLG working space, with every SDR project untouched.** In an HLG project every value between stages is an HLG signal over BT.2020, and every composition converts in BT.2020/HLG (M2, M8). An SDR project keeps today's arms, uniforms and composition colour, which every phase's H1 compare held byte-identical. (orig "The HLG working space (H-2, HD-2, HD-3; the brief's §2)"; HD-2)
41	- **The lift is Core Graphics' drawing, toe and all.** HD-3 fixed the lift as Core Graphics' CoreMedia709 → `itur_2100_HLG` (measured: SDR 0.50 → 0.5059), so a title and a recording of the same grey stay equal. H-2's P6, built to the pure γ, failed by 21 levels at grey 11/1023: Core Graphics decodes `max(s/16, s^γ)`. The lift took the toe, and the CPU lift then matched Core Graphics within 0.25 levels at all 1,024 greys. (orig H-2 "Found while building, and settled"; HD-3, HD-13)
42	- **The SDR version's knee sits at 0.9.** The brief's rows were recomputed on HD-3's lift. Report ITU-R BT.2408-9 was read before the knee was fixed: it gives no HDR → SDR curve or knee of its own (it points to BT.2446), so the knee stayed at 0.9 (a white title 248.4/255, HLG 0.50 125.7/255). (orig H-3; HD-4, HD-14)
43	- **One output pass, chosen by `dynamic_range`.** The SDR version and PQ are one final pass after the last layer, chosen by the recipe options of the key drawn, so the preview, `render_frame` and the export share one path. `export {dynamic_range}` (not `range`) defaults per row and refuses `hlg`/`pq` on an 8-bit row or in an SDR project. PQ never exceeds 1,000 cd/m², which makes HD-5's fixed metadata true. (orig "The deliverables (H-3, HD-4, HD-5, HD-7; the brief's §2)", H-3; HD-5, HD-14)
44	- **The scopes read the picture shown.** Under Show SDR Version, `render_frame {sdr_version}` and a JPEG, the scopes read the SDR version as an SDR project's, because they measure the deliverable on screen; Show Ungraded keeps the HLG reading. A 0/1 `signal` uniform picks Rec. 709's or BT.2020's constants, so the SDR arm stays T4-0's arithmetic. (orig H-4; HD-8, HD-15)
45	- **Linear means the project's own transfer, behind a switch.** `canvas.blending` is off for every project (GR-3 stands). On, the decode is the sRGB EOTF in SDR and HLG's inverse OETF in HLG, as scene light with no OOTF. It runs once per layer after the effects block, and the output pass encodes. The adjustment pass and the qualifier map read encoded values, and Show Selection's grey, a luma matte, the key and the scopes keep their meaning. (orig "Linear light (H-6, HD-9; the brief's §4)", H-6; HD-9, HD-16)
46	- **Canon from Canon's paper, Cinema Gamut from the ACES CSC.** The curves come from Canon's *Canon Log Gamma Curves* white paper (November 1st, 2018), read in place and never copied. Cinema Gamut's chromaticities come from the ACES project's Canon CSC (Apache-2.0), with no code copied and the matrices derived by `InputConversions.rgbToXYZ`. The code domain is (1, 0) in both ranges, as Apple Log's under GR-22. (orig H-5; HD-10, HD-17)
47	- **H-6 ran before H-5.** H-5 waited on Canon's document, and H-6 needed nothing H-5 adds, so under HD-11 H-6 took format 24 and H-5 format 25. (orig H-6; HD-16 (j))
48	- **The Concat rule held** at design and build time: nothing of Concat was opened. The sources were ITU-R BT.2100, BT.2408, BT.2390, BT.2020 and BT.709, SMPTE ST 2084, ST 2086 and CTA-861.3, ITU-T H.265's SEI syntax, Canon's published Canon Log documents, the ACES project's Canon CSC for Cinema Gamut's chromaticities, and Apple's conversions measured as targets, never copied. (orig "The Concat rule")

78	## Known limits
79	
80	- **Synthetic fixtures only.** No owner HDR or log clip reached the road map; real footage is HDR-1…HDR-6, LIN-1 and GRD-16, GRD-17, GRD-19's.
81	- **HD-2's named risk:** if HDR-1 finds the XDR panel shows the HLG preview tone-mapped rather than in EDR, the first fallback is setting the preview layer's `preferredDynamicRange` explicitly, then a `CAMetalLayer` preview, which would amend the `AVPlayerLayer` decision and is the owner's call.
82	- **An HDR still is read by an HLG- or PQ-based colour space** (HD-19 (a)), **or by an ISO or Apple HDR gain map, in an HLG project only** (HD-22): a gain-map photo's un-gained parts are the base's own light, not HD-3's lift of its codes, and its SDR version is the rendition toned down, not the photo's own base (owner's choices). Only a synthetic gain map was measured; a real iPhone photo, Apple's pre-ISO map and JPEG or AVIF gain maps are HDR-7's. A key picked on a gain-map still in an SDR project is close, not exact, after the switch to HLG (HD-22 (g)).
83	- **The key's SDR reading is close, not exact, in two cases** (HD-19 (c)): HLG over P3 or BT.709 (its working colour was matrixed in scene light) and PQ above 1,000 cd/m² (BT.2390's EETF is not undone). A Camera Log clip's key reads its SDR colour since HD-20 (#324).
84	- **Apple's own conversion ignores the peak:** M5's digest `d34d90b3f676a425` for the 600 and 1,000 cd/m² files, and H-1's unscored reading of all seven files (worst |Δ| 0 against `pq_plain`).
85	- **AV1's peak is measured without a decode:** P10 reads libsvtav1 files through `MediaImporter.detectedPQ` on an M2 Max, which refuses AV1 imports; an AV1 file's import, render and Media-tab section on an M3 or later Mac is HDR-4's step 7.
86	- **A video-range-flagged non-ProRes Canon file storing full-range codes reads too contrasty** (HD-17 (e); GRD-19).
87	- **No log detection** from the makers' metadata (#278).
88	- **No re-read of the peak on relink, or for a file imported before format 22** (HD-12).
89	- **The output pass's cost** did not show against two runs' noise (TO −0.040 ms); it is not resolved.
90	- **LB's 0.5 grey sits on a rounding boundary** of the SDR frame path: encoded 127.5 against linear 126.5, inside ±1/255.
91	- **The reverse's intermediate digest** differed from the control's in every phase, printed and unscored; its renders were byte-identical.
92	- **Timings** come from one M2 Max on a loaded host and are recorded, not budgets.
