# HDR: the PQ peak, the HLG timeline, its deliverables and scopes, linear light, Canon Log (road map "hdr")

- **Status:** Built and closed 2026-10-20. Each phase was one litecode pipeline with its own review, worked in `~/devel/framejob-hdr` on branch `hdr` and merged into main alone after its gate (HD-11). H-6 ran before H-5 (HD-16 (j)), so H-6 took format 24 and H-5 format 25:
  - H-0, the road map, HD-1…HD-11 and two pure moves (`ExportSheetCommit.swift`, `MediaImporter+Thumbnails.swift`) (`dcd08f3`)
  - H-1, #281: an HDR10 file's PQ white placed at its own peak (HD-6, HD-12, format 22) (`d93ece2`, the toll; `ec08cb9`)
  - H-2, #277 part 1: the HLG working space (HD-2, HD-3, HD-13, format 23) (`7aef1e8`)
  - H-3, #277 part 2: the deliverables — HLG, HDR10 and the SDR version (HD-4, HD-5, HD-7, HD-14) (`2540545`, the toll; `b2c247c`)
  - H-4, #277 part 3: HDR scopes (HD-8, HD-15) (`fe551cc`)
  - H-6, #276: linear-light blending as an opt-in project switch (GR-18, HD-9, HD-16, format 24) (`f35e56d`)
  - H-5, #278: Canon Log 2 and Canon Log 3, with Cinema Gamut or BT.2020 (HD-10, HD-17, format 25) (`13ccb1f`, Canon's paper ignored by git; `105ac08`)
  - H-7, the close: this record (the commit that moved this record to `archive/`)
- **Original:** `archive/hdr.md` is the full record. It has no section numbers, so it is cited by its own headings: "orig H-2" is its "H-2 — #277, the HLG working space (HD-2, HD-3, HD-13)" section.
- **Spec decisions:** HD-1..HD-17 in spec §11 (`designs/spec/11-decisions/hdr.md`). They stay binding, and where the original words them differently, §11's text wins:
  - HD-1: the road map builds everything (owner, 2026-10-19, choice 1a): #281, #277 in three phases (the working space, the deliverables, the scopes), #278's curves, #276 last and the first to drop, then the close; #274 only if a real clip is at hand.
  - HD-2: an HLG project: `canvas.output` `sdr`/`hlg`, BT.2020 HLG-encoded values with PR-1's clamps and encoded blending, every composition converting in BT.2020/HLG, step 0's HLG arms, drawn layers lifted at upload, BT.2020 luma and HLG's transfer in the grade, frames 16-bit labelled BT.2100 HLG, every SDR project byte-identical; format 23.
  - HD-3: SDR white fixed at 203 cd/m² (HLG 0.75), no setting; one lift for every SDR source and drawn layer, Core Graphics' `kCGColorSpaceCoreMedia709` → `itur_2100_HLG` (SDR 0.50 → 0.5059, 1.00 → 0.7500).
  - HD-4: the SDR version is the inverse of the lift with a shoulder above reference white (choice 3a).
  - HD-5: the deliverables: HLG on the 10-bit rows by default, HLG · HDR10 · SDR chosen per export, the SDR version on every other row and JPEG, Dolby Vision off, HDR10 metadata fixed (P3-D65, 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000, MaxFALL 0).
  - HD-6: #281: the PQ peak read at import (the format description, else the first sample's SEI 137/144), MaxCLL over the mastering maximum, an override, PQ white = peak/203, unknown 1,000; thumbnails follow; B96's evidence corrected; format 22.
  - HD-7: View ▸ Show SDR Version, the preview only, with a corner tag; `render_frame {sdr_version}`.
  - HD-8: HDR scopes in an HLG project: HLG % with a cd/m² scale, a 75 % reference line, clip marks at 100 %, the BT.2020 vectorscope; the JSON names its scale.
  - HD-9: #276 built last as GR-18 wrote it (`canvas.blending`); in an HLG project its decode is HLG's scene light.
  - HD-10: #278: Canon Log 2 and Canon Log 3 with Cinema Gamut under GR-16's recipe; S-Log3/V-Log detection waits for real files.
  - HD-11: the working arrangement: the `hdr` worktree, each phase gated and merged alone, main's next format numbers and HD IDs, no verdict phase, synthetic fixtures with real clips as manual checks, agents listing the `CLAUDE.md` edits owed.
  - HD-12: #281's key `media.color.pq {file?, from?, peak?}`, `set_media_color {color: {peak}}` and its three refusals, the `input`'s and the marker's `peak`, the Media tab's HDR10 section, `rc_hdr10_peak`, no re-read on relink or for a pre-22 file.
  - HD-13: H-2's settlements: the lift with Core Graphics' toe, the SDR, PQ (BT.2390's EETF above 1,000 cd/m²), HLG and camera-log arms, layers lifted at upload, the grade's BT.2020 constants, the key and a luma matte through the inverse lift, frames, the 10-bit rows tagged HLG, the words, two limits filed.
  - HD-14: H-3's settlements: the knee at 0.9, one output pass chosen by the key's `dynamic_range`, `export {dynamic_range}` and its refusals, PQ at 1,000 cd/m² with HD-5's two blobs, frames and JPEG the SDR version, Show SDR Version's key, the sheet's Dynamic Range row.
  - HD-15: H-4's settlements: the scopes read the picture shown, the signal from the recipe canvas, a 0/1 `signal` uniform, the 0/10/51/203/1000 cd/m² labels and the dashed 75 % line, BT.2111's bars and the lifted skin line, the HLG JSON and captions.

  - HD-17: H-5's settlements: Canon Log 2 and 3 from Canon's *Canon Log Gamma Curves* white paper, Cinema Gamut from the ACES project's Canon CSC (owner, 2026-10-20), each curve with Cinema Gamut or BT.2020, reflection 0.9 × scene linear, the code domain (1, 0) in both ranges, step 0's kinds 10 and 11, format 25.

## Context

Grading tier 3 converted HDR footage to Rec. 709 at step 0 and deferred the rest: GR-18 linear light (#276), GR-19 the HDR timeline (#277), and two items filed at its close, #278 (more log curves and their detection) and #281 (PQ's shoulder fixed at 1,000 cd/m² whatever the file says). On 2026-10-19 the owner said "Push. For 299, go with your recommendation. Then start HDR." and answered the HDR brief (`~/.claude/litecode/framejob/hdr-brief/I-hdr.md`, outside the repo) with every choice as recommended: "Everything (Recommended)" for the scope, "Inverse of the lift (Recommended)" for the SDR version, "HLG + HDR10, DV off (Recommended)" for the deliverables, and Sony S-Log3, Panasonic V-Log and Canon C-Log2/3 for #278, of which only Canon's two curves were new. The road map took #281, #277, #278 and #276, and #274 only if a real clip came (none did). On 2026-10-20, when Canon's own Cinema Gamut paper turned out only to plot the triangle, the owner chose "Use ACES, both gamuts (Recommended)" (HD-17). (orig "The owner's choices", "The road map as answered", H-5)

## Decisions

- **The PQ peak is read by two routes, MaxCLL first.** AVFoundation reads a sample description's `mdcv`/`clli` but not the HEVC SEI, and files from ffmpeg, HandBrake or x265 carry the SEI only (M5). So import reads the description's two extensions first and, failing those, the first sample's prefix SEI 137/144, parsed from bytes by a pure core reader (`rc_hdr10_peak`). The peak is MaxCLL when present and non-zero, else the mastering maximum, clamped to 10,000; unknown means 1,000, so every unlabelled file is byte-identical. Apple's own conversion ignores the metadata either way. (orig "#281 — the PQ peak (H-1, HD-6; the brief's §3)", H-1; HD-6, HD-12)
- **An HLG working space, with every SDR project untouched.** In an HLG project every value between stages is an HLG signal over BT.2020, and every composition converts in BT.2020/HLG (M2, M8). An SDR project keeps today's arms, uniforms and composition colour, which every phase's H1 compare held byte-identical. (orig "The HLG working space (H-2, HD-2, HD-3; the brief's §2)"; HD-2)
- **The lift is Core Graphics' drawing, toe and all.** HD-3 fixed the lift as Core Graphics' CoreMedia709 → `itur_2100_HLG` (measured: SDR 0.50 → 0.5059), so a title and a recording of the same grey stay equal. H-2's P6, built to the pure γ, failed by 21 levels at grey 11/1023: Core Graphics decodes `max(s/16, s^γ)`. The lift took the toe, and the CPU lift then matched Core Graphics within 0.25 levels at all 1,024 greys. (orig H-2 "Found while building, and settled"; HD-3, HD-13)
- **The SDR version's knee sits at 0.9.** The brief's rows were recomputed on HD-3's lift. Report ITU-R BT.2408-9 was read before the knee was fixed: it gives no HDR → SDR curve or knee of its own (it points to BT.2446), so the knee stayed at 0.9 (a white title 248.4/255, HLG 0.50 125.7/255). (orig H-3; HD-4, HD-14)
- **One output pass, chosen by `dynamic_range`.** The SDR version and PQ are one final pass after the last layer, chosen by the recipe options of the key drawn, so the preview, `render_frame` and the export share one path. `export {dynamic_range}` (not `range`) defaults per row and refuses `hlg`/`pq` on an 8-bit row or in an SDR project. PQ never exceeds 1,000 cd/m², which makes HD-5's fixed metadata true. (orig "The deliverables (H-3, HD-4, HD-5, HD-7; the brief's §2)", H-3; HD-5, HD-14)
- **The scopes read the picture shown.** Under Show SDR Version, `render_frame {sdr_version}` and a JPEG, the scopes read the SDR version as an SDR project's, because they measure the deliverable on screen; Show Ungraded keeps the HLG reading. A 0/1 `signal` uniform picks Rec. 709's or BT.2020's constants, so the SDR arm stays T4-0's arithmetic. (orig H-4; HD-8, HD-15)
- **Linear means the project's own transfer, behind a switch.** `canvas.blending` is off for every project (GR-3 stands). On, the decode is the sRGB EOTF in SDR and HLG's inverse OETF in HLG, as scene light with no OOTF. It runs once per layer after the effects block, and the output pass encodes. The adjustment pass and the qualifier map read encoded values, and Show Selection's grey, a luma matte, the key and the scopes keep their meaning. (orig "Linear light (H-6, HD-9; the brief's §4)", H-6; HD-9, HD-16)
- **Canon from Canon's paper, Cinema Gamut from the ACES CSC.** The curves come from Canon's *Canon Log Gamma Curves* white paper (November 1st, 2018), read in place and never copied. Cinema Gamut's chromaticities come from the ACES project's Canon CSC (Apache-2.0), with no code copied and the matrices derived by `InputConversions.rgbToXYZ`. The code domain is (1, 0) in both ranges, as Apple Log's under GR-22. (orig H-5; HD-10, HD-17)
- **H-6 ran before H-5.** H-5 waited on Canon's document, and H-6 needed nothing H-5 adds, so under HD-11 H-6 took format 24 and H-5 format 25. (orig H-6; HD-16 (j))
- **The Concat rule held** at design and build time: nothing of Concat was opened. The sources were ITU-R BT.2100, BT.2408, BT.2390, BT.2020 and BT.709, SMPTE ST 2084, ST 2086 and CTA-861.3, ITU-T H.265's SEI syntax, Canon's published Canon Log documents, the ACES project's Canon CSC for Cinema Gamut's chromaticities, and Apple's conversions measured as targets, never copied. (orig "The Concat rule")

## Known limits

- **Synthetic fixtures only.** No owner HDR or log clip reached the road map; real footage is HDR-1…HDR-6, LIN-1 and GRD-16, GRD-17, GRD-19's.
- **HD-2's named risk:** if HDR-1 finds the XDR panel shows the HLG preview tone-mapped rather than in EDR, the first fallback is setting the preview layer's `preferredDynamicRange` explicitly, then a `CAMetalLayer` preview, which would amend the `AVPlayerLayer` decision and is the owner's call.
- **An HDR still is read by an HLG- or PQ-based colour space** (HD-19 (a)), **or by an ISO or Apple HDR gain map, in an HLG project only** (HD-22): a gain-map photo's un-gained parts are the base's own light, not HD-3's lift of its codes, and its SDR version is the rendition toned down, not the photo's own base (owner's choices). Only a synthetic gain map was measured; a real iPhone photo, Apple's pre-ISO map and JPEG or AVIF gain maps are HDR-7's. A key picked on a gain-map still in an SDR project is close, not exact, after the switch to HLG (HD-22 (g)).
- **The key's SDR reading is close, not exact, in two cases** (HD-19 (c)): HLG over P3 or BT.709 (its working colour was matrixed in scene light) and PQ above 1,000 cd/m² (BT.2390's EETF is not undone). A Camera Log clip's key reads its SDR colour since HD-20 (#324).
- **Apple's own conversion ignores the peak:** M5's digest `d34d90b3f676a425` for the 600 and 1,000 cd/m² files, and H-1's unscored reading of all seven files (worst |Δ| 0 against `pq_plain`).
- **AV1's peak is measured without a decode:** P10 reads libsvtav1 files through `MediaImporter.detectedPQ` on an M2 Max, which refuses AV1 imports; an AV1 file's import, render and Media-tab section on an M3 or later Mac is HDR-4's step 7.

- **No log detection** from the makers' metadata (#278).
- **No re-read of the peak on relink, or for a file imported before format 22** (HD-12).
- **The output pass's cost** did not show against two runs' noise (TO −0.040 ms); it is not resolved.
- **LB's 0.5 grey sits on a rounding boundary** of the SDR frame path: encoded 127.5 against linear 126.5, inside ±1/255.
- **The reverse's intermediate digest** differed from the control's in every phase, printed and unscored; its renders were byte-identical.

1	# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)
2	
3	**Opened 2026-10-30** (AP0), when the owner answered the five choices below ("Yes, lift scopes,
4	and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the rest): AU-2…AU-4, and spec
5	§1's audio non-goal lifted. The brief
6	is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
7	`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
8	AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).
9	
10	## Goal
11	
12	Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
13	a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
14	turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
15	can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
16	then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
17	hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
18	buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
19	MCP mirror, as every control does today.
20	
21	## What it delivers first
22	
23	The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
24	loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
25	(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
26	Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
27	Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
28	−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
29	limiter and the target.
30	
31	## The owner's choices (answered 2026-10-30: all five as recommended)
32	
33	Recorded as AU-2 (choice 1), AU-3 (choices 4 and 5) and AU-4 (choices 2 and 3). The owner,
34	on the rest: "We'll address other questions as we progress. If builds can be run in multiple
35	lanes, do so."
36	
37	1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
38	   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
39	   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
40	2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
41	   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
42	3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
43	   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
44	   *Recommended.*
45	4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
46	   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,
47	   deterministic, testable against analytic responses. Apple's units only where Frame Job cannot
48	   write its own: ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`) and E8's voice effects, both rendered

# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)

**Opened 2026-10-30** (AP0), when the owner answered the five choices below ("Yes, lift scopes,
and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the rest): AU-2…AU-4, and spec
§1's audio non-goal lifted. The brief
is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).

## Goal

Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
MCP mirror, as every control does today.

## What it delivers first

The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
limiter and the target.

## The owner's choices (answered 2026-10-30: all five as recommended)

Recorded as AU-2 (choice 1), AU-3 (choices 4 and 5) and AU-4 (choices 2 and 3). The owner,
on the rest: "We'll address other questions as we progress. If builds can be run in multiple
lanes, do so."

1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
   *Recommended.*
4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,
   deterministic, testable against analytic responses. Apple's units only where Frame Job cannot
   write its own: ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`) and E8's voice effects, both rendered
   offline as speed-ramp audio is. AP0's spike S1 confirms or overturns this. *Recommended.*
5. **One fixed chain order, not a user-ordered list.** Channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch
   → isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, each stage off by
   default and inert when off. A closed vocabulary like every other effect (§11 R5-1), and the
   order an engineer would choose for voice. *Recommended.*

Asked later, at the phase that needs them (each has a recommendation there): how the volume
line is edited (AP8), the split-edit model (AP9), track processing in the preview and the stem
format (AP10), and where speech spans live for ducking (AP11).

  runs 104–475× real time but lags edits. In the export, one reader with one mix output per
  timeline track gives sub-mixes that sum to the mix within −147.7 dB, so track and bus dynamics,
  the master chain and stems are exact there. Summing the existing taps by timestamp, each times
  the plan's envelope, matches the export's mix within 0.0067 LU momentary; today's sum of
  per-track peaks over-reads the true peak by up to 3.85 dB. `AVAssetWriter` writes multitrack
  `.mov`/`.mp4` stems (AAC or 24-bit LPCM) that AVFoundation and ffprobe read.
- **S4, the loudness cache — 10 ms blocks.** Against the export's own meter fed exactly the window:
  100 ms blocks miss by up to −0.139 LU, 25 ms by −0.149, 10 ms stay within 0.076 (97.5 % of 200
  random windows within 0.1 LU; the rest is where BS.1770's 400 ms grid falls, which moves the
  export's own figure by a median 0.17 LU). 10 ms is the peaks grid, so `MediaPeaks.window`,
  `ReverseMirror` and the source map apply unchanged. Records are Float32 per block (mono `z, tp`;
  stereo `zL, zR, zLR, tpL, tpR`, which answers any 2×2 channel matrix): 2.75 MB/h mono, 6.9 MB/h
  stereo, built at about 1 s per 20 minutes. Gating blocks are counted from the exact window length;
  a reversed clip's grid starts at the forward window's end; a ramped clip is measured on its ×1
  render. **The export copies a mono clip into both channels, +3.01 LU**: the owner's recording is
  −41.67 LUFS as exported (−44.7 is the mono file's own figure), and Normalize must use the
  exported figure. Speech-only loudness reads 1.1–1.7 LU above gated BS.1770 here; AU-4's gated
  target stands.
- **S1, own DSP or Apple's units live — own; AU-3 stands, no amendment.** The rule, fixed before
  the runs: a subject is admissible for a live stage when it allocates and locks nothing on the
  tap's thread, reads byte-identically twice AND whatever the buffer sizes, is within 0.1 dB of
  its analytic response (a limiter within 0.1 dB of a −1 dBTP ceiling), has one constant latency
  ≤ 512 samples, and an eight-stage stereo chain costs ≤ 1 % of real time. Frame Job's own stages
  (Double RBJ biquads, an expander, the shipped compressor, a lookahead true-peak limiter) pass all
  five; no Apple unit passes for any stage. Apple's output depends on how the stream is cut into
  render calls — at rounding level for `AUNBandEQ` and `AUPeakLimiter` (−145 to −223 dBFS), up to
  −34 dBFS for `AUDynamicsProcessor` on irregular slices, which `AudioTap`'s splits at cuts and the
  player's 4096-frame against the reader's 512-frame buffers both make. `AUPeakLimiter` limits
  sample peak at a fixed 0 dBFS (+3.10 dBTP on a crest signal, +2.10 with −1 dB after it) and its
  latency is its attack (48–1440 samples). `AUNBandEQ` is exactly the RBJ cookbook, but only
  1.5–1.6× cheaper than own biquads (under the 2× bar), its stacked high-passes make a
  Linkwitz-Riley slope, not Butterworth, and it smooths a parameter change itself over 3–27 ms. The
  own chain of eight stages costs 107.5 µs per 1024 stereo frames (0.50 % of real time); every own
  stage adds no latency but the limiter, 158 samples (3.3 ms at a 2 ms lookahead). Apple's units
  *can* run in the tap without allocating or locking (v2 `AudioUnitRender`; v3 only with its
  input bus enabled and block-typed calls); the record keeps that recipe. The tap's thread is
  AudioToolbox's real-time thread on the export's path too.

**What it changes in the phases.** AP1 measures the exported figure (mono counted twice). AP2's
master limiter in the export's float stage is required, not optional — two clips each under their
own limiter reached +1.49 dBTP through a crossfade — and the preview has none, which the guide and
the meter say. AP5 follows S2's recipe and moves isolation ahead of the live chain. AP7 rebuilds
the mix from the taps off the audio thread. AP10 labels each composition span with its timeline
track (and inner track), makes track dynamics exact in the export through per-track sub-mixes and
approximate in the preview, and asks the owner whether an exact preview (the `AVAudioEngine`
route) is wanted as a road map of its own.

From S1, for every live stage (AP2, AP3, AP4): scalar per-sample code or element-wise vDSP only —
`vDSP_biquad` and `vDSP_conv` give different bits for different buffer sizes; an FIR loops its taps
outermost (bit-identical to the scalar loop and 4.7× faster); a stage's `reset()` restores its fresh
state and `AudioTap` keeps resetting on StartOfStream, because the player's first callback is a
silent pre-roll that otherwise leaves a gate closed (−56 dBFS off the export). AP2's limiter takes
the maximum over a 64-tap Kaiser (β 10) detector's phases AND BS.1770 Annex 2's: a detector the
size of Annex 2's alone lets broadband onsets through up to +0.97 dB, while Annex 2 over-reads
speech by 0.14 dB, so a limiter exact by an accurate meter is reported at −0.86 dBTP by
`Loudness.swift` and `phase5_proof.py`. Like the noise reducer, it runs for the whole track once
any clip on it asks, so the track's delay never changes at a cut (670 samples with both).

then real audio from 963072; the tap places the first in the live meter, so the meter sums 4096
frames of silence at [960000, 964096). Replacing those frames of the levelled export with silence
gives −23.2635 LUFS, the meter's reading to four places. It is the meter's, not the leveller's:
the unprocessed clip seeking to 25 s (loud speech) reads −0.0385 LU, and to 20 s 0.0000 only
because the quiet segment there falls under the relative gate; the leveller lifts it over. Not
placing a zero-duration buffer fixes P3 (both seeks 0.0000) but makes `audio_ap7_proof.py`'s L3
(pause and continue, AU-72) reset on the resume, 5375 frames ahead, so it is filed, not fixed
here. The row now holds the leveller's own part against a CONTROL on the same plays — the
levelled export placed as a clip with nothing on it, in a project of its own, against its own
export — its signed ΔI less the control's within 0.01 LU (AU-67 (e)); the first play's row stays
absolute.

**Measured** (the continuation; three lanes shared the machine). On Debug, `audio_ap6b_proof.py
P2` 6/6: P2 (b) worst 2.408 dB, P3 the first play ΔI +0.0000 LU, the seek −0.0041 LU levelled and
−0.0041 LU the control, the leveller's own −0.0000. `--mutants` 15/15 again on the final probe;
M11 by hand failed `a_leveller_named_by_an_end_is_in_the_points` (9/10), restored 10/10. `make
gate` PASS 84 s (names 1 s, test 82 s, the rest skipped as unchanged). Against Release:
`audio_ap6b_proof.py` 34/34 — P2 (a) 13.63 LU in, 2.32 out, (b) worst 2.408 dB, (c) 0.000 dB,
(d) 0.000 dB outside; P3 the first play ΔI +0.0000 LU, the seek −0.0040 LU levelled and −0.0040
LU the control, the leveller's own −0.0000; P4 the leveller on (13.1 LU), the export −16.00 LUFS
at −0.9999 / −0.9999 dBTP, the last verify −15.998, presses 2 and 3 "made no change"; P5 the
leveller null (2.1 LU), Enhance and three Normalize rounds −21.28278599304145 (spread 0.00000);
P6 the owner's 4.67 LU, null, a second call "made no change"; P7 +0.000 / −6.000 dB; P8 the six
rows and "Aims at −20.7 LUFS". `audio_ap6_proof.py` 37/37 (V1 the nine keys, V2 −15.98 LUFS),
`audio_ap6c_proof.py` 39/39, `loudness_normalize_proof.py` 37/37, `audio_ap12_proof.py` 16/16,
`audio_ap8b_proof.py` 16/16, `screens.py --only 09-clip-sound,09c-clip-sound-dynamics` 7 pass, 0
fail, 0 new problems; the instance's log printed no `Frame Job: ` line.

**Review.** The first review asked one fix: AU-67 (e) and its index row named mutants M1–M10 and
M12–M17 and rows R1–R4, where the probe runs fifteen (M16 has no edit, AU-64 (i)) and has R5; the
fix pass (`8de7212`, three spec files) corrected both and their Lines cells (`spec_index_proof.py`
213/213, `make gate` PASS 246 s). The second review passed with three nits, kept: the guide gives
the owner's speech range as 4.6 LU where the app's Enhance reason reads 4.7 (4.672); the Status
gives "no phrase with 1 s of speech" also for a reading whose step count the segments do not
match, which cannot happen today; and the curve memo is keyed by the plan text, so editing Target
or a cap on a clip with an action remakes its curves (≤ 100 ms per hour, L8), where AU-66 (e) says
they remake nothing.

**Integrated.** Nothing had landed since the lane's base, so the four commits applied clean;
format 37 and SE-41 keep their numbers. The CLAUDE.md edits owed went in: app's map names
`AudioLevellerCurve.swift` and `AudioLevellerStage.swift` (a new entry), the tap's ten effects
and its leveller, `AudioDSPParameters(snapshot:levels:curves:)`, the held response,
`LevellerProps`, `AudioDynamicsLevels`' curves and `speech` posts, the Leveller section and
`AudioEnhance+Leveller`; core's map names `Leveller` (format 37), `check_leveller` /
`clamp_leveller`, the fifth held number and the twelfth tap key. On the merged tree `make gate`
PASS 347 s (names 1, typecheck 7 with the four baseline warnings, fmt 3, lint 10, test 193, app
133); no product code was resolved, so the lane's Release proofs stand.

**Owed.** SE-41 for the owner; the meter's seek filler, filed as an issue.

### Closing the road map

The ADR in `designs/adr/audio.md`, this file and the survey archived with their rows in
`archive/INDEX.md`, the guide pages and README highlights, and every unfinished item filed as an
issue.

## Risks

- **CPU in the live tap.** Up to eight stages per clip on every composition track, real-time.
  S1 measured eight own stages at 0.50 % of real time per stereo track; a stage that cannot run
  live renders offline as isolation does.
- **Preview against export.** Master processing may exist only in the export (S3). If so, the
  guide and the meter say so rather than leave the two to differ silently.
- **Offline renders.** Isolation and voice effects add render time and cache space; both reuse
  the ramp-audio queue's owners, waits and pruning.
- **ML determinism.** If `AUSoundIsolation` is not byte-repeatable, its proofs measure levels
  and alignment, not bytes.
- **Format bumps.** AP3, AP4, AP8, AP9, AP10 and AP11 each add persisted fields; each bump has
  its `schema_vN.rs` test.
- **File caps.** `AudioDSP.swift` (890) and `Loudness.swift` (674) are over the 600-line cap
  and `AudioTap.swift` (595) is at it; `model_props.rs` (551) is close. AP0's tolls come
  first, and each later phase budgets its own.

## Not in this road map

Tier C (beat detection, retiming music, source separation, AI speech, third-party plug-in
hosting, round-trips to an audio editor, automatic tagging, a spectrum analyser, sample-level
repair, surround) and anything the owner's answers move out.

1	# Audio survey: what professional editors offer, and what Frame Job lacks
2	
3	- **Status:** Survey, 2026-10-30. Proposals only: nothing here is a spec §11
4	  decision. A phase that takes one up records it in
5	  `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (the AU- series, begun by AU-1) before
6	  its code.
7	- **The question (owner, 2026-10-30):** "Review the audio editing features of
8	  other video editing tools. What other audio editing features should we
9	  support to be considered a professional-grade tool?"
10	- **The immediate case:** a quiet but clean RØDE USB desktop-microphone voice
11	  recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, which the owner wants to turn into
12	  usable audio for videos. §2 measures it, and §5 marks which gaps it needs
13	  first.
14	- **Method:** every claim about another editor cites the vendor's own manual,
15	  help page, new-features guide or release notes (§7). Three limits on that:
16	  - **Adobe:** helpx.adobe.com refused direct fetches (HTTP 403). Premiere
17	    claims are therefore taken from search-engine excerpts of the cited
18	    helpx pages, not from a full read.
19	  - **Blackmagic:** the DaVinci Resolve Reference Manual (thousands of pages)
20	    was not read. Resolve claims come from Blackmagic's New Features Guides
21	    for 19, 19.1 and 20, and from its product and What's New pages.
22	  - **CapCut:** it publishes no help pages for its audio tools that I could
23	    find. Its claims come from CapCut's own marketing articles and are marked
24	    *unverified*.
25	
26	  Apple framework claims were checked against developer.apple.com and the
27	  macOS 26.2 SDK headers.
28	
29	## Contents
30	
31	1. [Frame Job today](#1-frame-job-today)
32	2. [The owner's recording, measured](#2-the-owners-recording-measured)
33	3. [What the other editors offer](#3-what-the-other-editors-offer)
34	4. [Feature matrix](#4-feature-matrix)
35	5. [The gaps, tiered](#5-the-gaps-tiered)
36	6. [Sample recordings to add](#6-sample-recordings-to-add)
37	7. [Sources](#7-sources)
38	
39	## Spec §1's non-goals, and the flags below
40	
41	Spec §1 (`designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md`) lists as a deliberate non-goal
42	"audio beyond what shipped (volume, fades, duck, pan, compressor, noise
43	reduction, peak normalize, the transition crossfade and the export's loudness
44	target — M3 and §11 R5-2; so no EQ, mix buses or Audio Units, while offline
45	voice effects are deferred rather than out)". The same section sets the bar
46	"without Final Cut's magnetic timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin
47	ecosystem", and lists "a plugin system" (§11 G-1) as a non-goal.
48	
49	Every proposal below goes beyond "what shipped", and the owner's audio pass
50	has already begun lifting that umbrella clause (AU-1 raised the volume
51	ceiling). Each gap is therefore flagged only against the **named** items:
52	
53	| Flag | Non-goal it would lift |
54	|---|---|
55	| **NG-EQ** | "no EQ" |
56	| **NG-BUS** | "no … mix buses" |
57	| **NG-AU** | "no … Audio Units". This survey reads it as *hosting Audio Units as a feature*. Frame Job already runs one of Apple's units internally: `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` renders speed-ramp audio (`app/Sources/RampAudioRenderer+TimePitch.swift`). A gap built on an Apple unit is marked **NG-AU?** for the owner to rule on. |
58	| **NG-ROLES** | "roles" (the §1 bar) |
59	| **NG-PLUGIN** | "a plugin system" (§11 G-1) |
60	| **E8** | "offline voice effects are deferred rather than out" (issue #123) |
61	
62	## 1. Frame Job today
63	
64	Written from the guide pages, which are written from the code.
65	
66	| Area | What exists | Guide |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| Clip level | Volume 0–3200 % (slider 0–400 %, field to 3200 %, AU-1); Mute; gain read-out in dB | `docs/guide/audio.md` |
69	| Normalize | Peak only: sets Volume so the clip's loudest moment over the played range, read from its cached waveform, reaches −1 dBFS (agents: `peak_db` −60…0). Each clip separately; no matching across clips | audio.md |
70	| Fades | Fade in and out, 0–10 s, straight-line ramps; handles on the clip | audio.md |
71	| Ducking | Lowers every *other* clip while this one is on the timeline: Level, Attack, Release. Follows the clip's extent, not voice activity | audio.md |
72	| Noise reduction | One Amount (0–100 %). Profiles steady noise from the clip itself ("hiss, hum and fan noise"); not a gate; doesn't remove sudden sounds | audio.md |
73	| Compressor | Threshold −60…0 dB (default −18), ratio 1–20:1, attack 0–200 ms, release 10–2000 ms, makeup 0–24 dB. Acts *before* Volume | audio.md |
74	| Mix | Pan (a balance on stereo; a true pan with Mix to mono); Mix to mono (averages channels) | audio.md |
75	| Detach Audio | Splits sound onto its own clip on the track below. One way: no control re-links or re-enables it (Undo, or an agent's `set_enabled`) | audio.md, `editing.md` |
76	| Speed | Keep pitch (on by default); ramp and tape-speed audio rendered offline; no sound above ×12 | `speed.md` |
77	| Transitions | Optional constant-power audio crossfade (R5-2) | audio.md |
78	| Tracks | Mute, Solo. No track volume, pan or effects | audio.md |
79	| Animation | Volume, Mute and the fades only, through actions on the clip's action lane. Pan, mono, Keep pitch, compressor, noise reduction and ducking can't be animated. Nothing is drawn on the waveform | audio.md, `timeline.md` |
80	| Metering | Live two-channel meter of the mix: RMS bar, peak wash, 1.2 s peak hold, clip cells, −60…0 dB. It shows peaks, not loudness. The recorder has its own microphone meter | audio.md |
81	| Export loudness | Optional integrated target (BS.1770-4): −14, −16, −23 or custom −70…0 LUFS, under a −1 dBTP ceiling (agents −20…0). **Gain only, no limiter**: "A target the ceiling will not allow lands quieter than asked." Every export reports its true peak and LUFS | `export.md` |
82	| Export formats | Stereo 48 kHz: AAC, Opus, or 16-bit LPCM in ProRes. Audio-only M4A, WAV and AIFF (WAV and AIFF are 16-bit only) | export.md |
83	| Sync | Synchronize Audio: MFCC/speech match, waveform gate, sub-frame offset, drift corrected up to 0.2 % | audio.md |
84	| Clean-up | Remove Silences (on-device voice model, or a level threshold); Remove Filler Words (AssemblyAI, bring-your-own key) | `cleanup-tools.md` |
85	| Recording | Microphone recorded as mono 48 kHz AAC, a separate file from system audio; voice-overs land on a new Microphone track. No processing at record time | `screen-recording.md` |
86	| Scrubbing | Silent: "Playback stops while you scrub" | timeline.md |
87	| Copying | Paste Attributes carries the whole sound setup | audio.md |
88	
89	Open issues on audio include #86 (decode the export mix as float, then offer
90	24-bit WAV and AIFF), #123 (E8 offline voice effects), and #299 (Keep pitch
91	timing).
92	
93	### How it is built, as far as it bears on feasibility
94	
95	- **Per-clip effects run in a tap, before the fader.** Pan, mono,
96	  compressor and noise reduction run in one `MTAudioProcessingTap` per
97	  composition audio track, created PreEffects [AD10]. Volume, fades and ducking
98	  come after it, as the plan's envelope applied as volume ramps
99	  (`app/Sources/AudioTap.swift`). A new per-clip stage therefore sees the
100	  clip at its recorded level, before Volume (up to ×32) is applied.
101	- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** Each track carries
102	  exactly one tap, and the metering build already uses it
103	  (`AudioTap.swift`). The export reads a 32-bit float mix and applies its
104	  loudness gain there (`app/Sources/ExporterAudioGain.swift`).
105	- **Heavy or pitch-changing work renders offline.** Speed-ramp audio is
106	  rendered offline into the package's `cache/` (`speed.md`). With Keep pitch
107	  on, that render drives Apple's `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` in `AVAudioEngine`'s
108	  offline manual rendering mode [AD9]
109	  (`app/Sources/RampAudioRenderer+TimePitch.swift`). E8's design (#123)
110	  measured the same pattern for Apple's effect units, because the live tap
111	  "cannot host a pitch shifter".
112	
113	## 2. The owner's recording, measured
114	
115	`samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`: 30.4 s, AAC mono, 48 kHz. Measured 2026-10-30
116	with ffmpeg's `astats` and `ebur128=peak=true` and a numpy pass over
117	50 ms windows and FFT bands. The script lived in a scratch folder and is not
118	in the tree.
119	
120	| Measure | Value |
121	|---|---|
122	| Sample peak / true peak | −18.6 dBFS / −18.5 dBTP |
123	| Integrated loudness | −44.7 LUFS |
124	| Loudness range (LRA) | 21.1 LU (LRA low −64.3 LUFS, high −43.1 LUFS) |
125	| 50 ms RMS, 10th percentile (the floor) | −64.3 dBFS |
126	| 50 ms RMS, 90th / 99th percentile (speech) | −43.2 / −35.8 dBFS |
127	| Windows within 6 dB of the floor | 65 % |
128	| Pause noise below 80 Hz / below 300 Hz | 20 % / 78 % of its energy |
129	| Tonal peaks at 50, 100 / 60, 120 Hz in pauses | 9–11 dB over neighbouring bins, in both mains families |
130	| 5–9 kHz vs 0.3–4 kHz on active windows | median −22.4 dB, 95th percentile −0.2 dB |
131	
132	What the numbers say:
133	
134	1. **Peak normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near
135	   −27 LUFS.** The peak-to-loudness ratio is 26 dB. Normalize to −1 dBFS
136	   applies +17.6 dB, so the clip lands at about −27.1 LUFS. A −16 LUFS
137	   target needs +28.7 dB and −14 LUFS needs +30.7 dB, which would put the
138	   true peak at about +10 or +12 dBTP. The export's gain is capped at the
139	   −1 dBTP ceiling, so the file lands at the same −27 LUFS, "quieter than
140	   asked". Reaching either target takes **about 11–13 dB of peak
141	   reduction**: a compressor and a limiter, not just gain.
142	2. **At its defaults, the shipped compressor never acts on this file.** Its
143	   threshold is −18 dB and it runs before Volume, while the file peaks at
144	   −18.6 dBFS. To use it here, a person has to know to drop the threshold
145	   to around −40 dB.
146	3. **The lift raises the floor into earshot.** After +28.7 dB, the pause
147	   floor sits around −36 dBFS, and the pauses fill 65 % of the 50 ms
148	   windows. The pause noise is low: 78 % of it lies below 300 Hz, but only
149	   20 % below 80 Hz. A high-pass at 80 Hz takes about 1 dB off it. The rest
150	   shares the voice's own range, so it needs noise reduction, voice
151	   isolation, or a downward expander that closes in the pauses.
152	4. **The 21 LU loudness range is the pauses, not the voice.** LRA's low end,
153	   −64.3 LUFS, *is* the noise floor: its −68.4 LUFS relative gate lets the
154	   quiet stretches in. A dialogue leveller is not this file's first need.
155	5. **Mains hum and sibilance are not indicated.** Both are inconclusive.
156	   The low bins rise by a similar amount in the 50 Hz and 60 Hz families,
157	   which reads as the low-frequency slope rather than a hum. Fricatives
158	   reach the voice band's energy in 5 % of active windows, which needs a
159	   listen. Sibilance matters more once EQ presence and heavy compression
160	   are added.
161	
162	Not measured: what the shipped noise reducer does to this file's floor.
163	That is the first comparison a phase should make, with Apple's
164	`AUSoundIsolation` as the other side (see A4).
165	
166	## 3. What the other editors offer
167	
168	Each line cites §7. "Studio" means Resolve's paid edition.
169	
170	### DaVinci Resolve (Fairlight, Edit and Cut pages)

Open issues on audio include #86 (decode the export mix as float, then offer
24-bit WAV and AIFF), #123 (E8 offline voice effects), and #299 (Keep pitch
timing).

### How it is built, as far as it bears on feasibility

- **Per-clip effects run in a tap, before the fader.** Pan, mono,
  compressor and noise reduction run in one `MTAudioProcessingTap` per
  composition audio track, created PreEffects [AD10]. Volume, fades and ducking
  come after it, as the plan's envelope applied as volume ramps
  (`app/Sources/AudioTap.swift`). A new per-clip stage therefore sees the
  clip at its recorded level, before Volume (up to ×32) is applied.
- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** Each track carries
  exactly one tap, and the metering build already uses it
  (`AudioTap.swift`). The export reads a 32-bit float mix and applies its
  loudness gain there (`app/Sources/ExporterAudioGain.swift`).
- **Heavy or pitch-changing work renders offline.** Speed-ramp audio is
  rendered offline into the package's `cache/` (`speed.md`). With Keep pitch
  on, that render drives Apple's `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` in `AVAudioEngine`'s
  offline manual rendering mode [AD9]
  (`app/Sources/RampAudioRenderer+TimePitch.swift`). E8's design (#123)
  measured the same pattern for Apple's effect units, because the live tap
  "cannot host a pitch shifter".

## 2. The owner's recording, measured

`samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`: 30.4 s, AAC mono, 48 kHz. Measured 2026-10-30
with ffmpeg's `astats` and `ebur128=peak=true` and a numpy pass over
50 ms windows and FFT bands. The script lived in a scratch folder and is not
in the tree.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Sample peak / true peak | −18.6 dBFS / −18.5 dBTP |
| Integrated loudness | −44.7 LUFS |
| Loudness range (LRA) | 21.1 LU (LRA low −64.3 LUFS, high −43.1 LUFS) |
| 50 ms RMS, 10th percentile (the floor) | −64.3 dBFS |
| 50 ms RMS, 90th / 99th percentile (speech) | −43.2 / −35.8 dBFS |
| Windows within 6 dB of the floor | 65 % |
| Pause noise below 80 Hz / below 300 Hz | 20 % / 78 % of its energy |
| Tonal peaks at 50, 100 / 60, 120 Hz in pauses | 9–11 dB over neighbouring bins, in both mains families |
| 5–9 kHz vs 0.3–4 kHz on active windows | median −22.4 dB, 95th percentile −0.2 dB |

What the numbers say:

1. **Peak normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near
   −27 LUFS.** The peak-to-loudness ratio is 26 dB. Normalize to −1 dBFS
   applies +17.6 dB, so the clip lands at about −27.1 LUFS. A −16 LUFS
   target needs +28.7 dB and −14 LUFS needs +30.7 dB, which would put the
   true peak at about +10 or +12 dBTP. The export's gain is capped at the
   −1 dBTP ceiling, so the file lands at the same −27 LUFS, "quieter than
   asked". Reaching either target takes **about 11–13 dB of peak
   reduction**: a compressor and a limiter, not just gain.
2. **At its defaults, the shipped compressor never acts on this file.** Its
   threshold is −18 dB and it runs before Volume, while the file peaks at
   −18.6 dBFS. To use it here, a person has to know to drop the threshold
   to around −40 dB.
3. **The lift raises the floor into earshot.** After +28.7 dB, the pause
   floor sits around −36 dBFS, and the pauses fill 65 % of the 50 ms
   windows. The pause noise is low: 78 % of it lies below 300 Hz, but only
   20 % below 80 Hz. A high-pass at 80 Hz takes about 1 dB off it. The rest
   shares the voice's own range, so it needs noise reduction, voice
   isolation, or a downward expander that closes in the pauses.
4. **The 21 LU loudness range is the pauses, not the voice.** LRA's low end,
   −64.3 LUFS, *is* the noise floor: its −68.4 LUFS relative gate lets the
   quiet stretches in. A dialogue leveller is not this file's first need.
5. **Mains hum and sibilance are not indicated.** Both are inconclusive.
   The low bins rise by a similar amount in the 50 Hz and 60 Hz families,
   which reads as the low-frequency slope rather than a hum. Fricatives
   reach the voice band's energy in 5 % of active windows, which needs a
   listen. Sibilance matters more once EQ presence and heavy compression
   are added.

Not measured: what the shipped noise reducer does to this file's floor.
That is the first comparison a phase should make, with Apple's
`AUSoundIsolation` as the other side (see A4).

## 5. The gaps, tiered

Each gap gives what it is, who has it, why it matters here, a one-line
feasibility note on Apple Silicon and macOS 26 (AVFoundation, no ffmpeg),
and any non-goal flag. **Mic** marks what `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a` needs,
per §2's measurements.

### What the quiet desktop-mic recording needs first

The order below follows the §2 measurements, not assumptions:

| Order | Gap | Why, from §2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A1 limiter and A2 loudness-target normalize, together | Peak normalize and the gain-only export target both stop near −27 LUFS; −16 or −14 LUFS needs 11–13 dB of peak reduction |
| 2 | B1 a voice preset chain | The compressor exists but is inert at its defaults on a −18.6 dBFS peak, because it runs before Volume |
| 3 | A5 expander, or A4 voice isolation, beside the shipped noise reduction | After the lift, the pause floor sits around −36 dBFS in 65 % of the windows |
| 4 | A3 high-pass and EQ | A standard step, though only about 1 dB here; presence and tone after that |
| Later | A6 de-esser, B3 leveller, A7 hum removal | Not indicated by the measurements: sibilance inconclusive, LRA is the pauses, no clear hum |

### Tier A: needed to be called professional-grade

**A1. A true-peak limiter, and an export loudness target that reaches its
number.** **Mic: first.**

- **What:** a lookahead, true-peak limiter on the clip strip and on the
  export's mix. The export's loudness stage limits instead of capping gain,
  so −14 LUFS means −14 LUFS.
- **Who:**
  - Resolve: the channel-strip limiter [R1], and Deliver's "Optimize
    loudness and peak" [R3].
  - FCP: Limiter and Adaptive Limiter [F4].
  - Premiere: Hard Limiter [P7], and Media Encoder's true-peak limiter
    inside loudness normalization [P9].
  - Descript: Limiter [D2].
  - ScreenFlow: peak limiting [S1].
- **Why:** quiet voice recordings have a high peak-to-loudness ratio (26 dB
  here), so gain alone hits the ceiling long before any streaming target.
- **Feasibility:** `AUPeakLimiter` exists (attack, decay, pre-gain
  −40…+40 dB) [AD3], but true-peak detection is not documented for it. A
  limiter written beside `AudioDSP.swift`'s compressor, oversampled, is the
  surer route. The mix stage belongs where the export already gains in
  float (`ExporterAudioGain.swift`). A clip limiter in the tap must carry
  the clip's gain itself, because Volume is applied after the tap. The
  preview has no post-mix insert, so a preview master limiter is an open
  design question.
- **Flags:** none named (it is dynamics, like the shipped compressor).
  **NG-AU?** if built on `AUPeakLimiter`.

**A2. Loudness-target clip normalization and level matching.** **Mic:
first.**

- **What:** "Normalize to −16 LUFS" per clip, measured over the played
  range with the BS.1770 gate, and optionally speech-only. Also "match these
  clips' loudness". A clip's measured LUFS is shown in the inspector.
- **Who:** Premiere Auto-Match, with the clip's LUFS displayed [P3]; Resolve
  clip normalization [R1] and the AI Level Matcher [R2]; Descript's LUFS
  export options [D4].
- **Why:** peak normalize lands this file at −27 LUFS while a louder take
  lands elsewhere. Loudness is what a viewer hears, and clips cut together
  need to match.
- **Feasibility:** the BS.1770-4 measurement already exists for the export
  (`Loudness.swift`, `ExporterLoudness.swift`). It needs only a per-clip
  read like Normalize's. The ×32 ceiling (AU-1) covers the gain, and A1
  catches the peaks.
- **Flags:** none named.

**A3. EQ: high-pass, low-pass, shelves and parametric bands, with voice
presets.** **Mic: fourth.**

- **Who:** every professional editor and two creator tools:
  - Resolve: a 6-band clip EQ and a track EQ with 24 dB/octave filters [R1,
    R2, R3].
  - FCP: Equalization presets, Channel EQ and Match [F1, F2, F4].
  - Premiere: Parametric Equalizer and Clarity EQ [P6, P7].
  - Descript: EQs and high-pass [D2].
  - ScreenFlow: EQ [S1].
- **Why:** desk mics pick up rumble, desk thumps and plosives, and EQ is
  the basic tone control. Several other gaps are built from it (A6, A7,
  B6).
- **Feasibility:** `AVAudioUnitEQ` offers parametric, low-pass, high-pass,
  shelf and band-stop types [AD7], and `AUNBandEQ` the same per band [AD6].
  Biquads in the tap are cheap DSP of Frame Job's own and stay live.
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ**.

**A4. ML voice isolation (speech enhancement).** **Mic: third (with A5).**

- **Who:** FCP Voice Isolation [F1]; Resolve Voice Isolation (Studio) [R2,
  R6]; Premiere Enhance Speech [P1]; Descript Studio Sound (cloud) [D1];
  Camtasia AI Noise Removal [T3]; CapCut Enhance voice (*unverified*) [C2].
- **Why:** this is now the baseline one-control fix for noisy rooms and
  cheap microphones, and the creator audience expects it. Frame Job's
  reducer handles only steady noise.
- **Feasibility:** Apple's `AUSoundIsolation` runs on the device (macOS
  13+). Its parameters are a wet/dry mix and a sound type; the
  HighQualityVoice model needs macOS 15+ [AD1]. Render it offline into
  `cache/`, as speed-ramp audio is, with a wet/dry Amount. Its latency, CPU
  cost and quality on this file are unmeasured.
- **Flags:** **NG-AU?**

**A5. Downward expander or noise gate.** **Mic: third.**

- **Who:** Resolve's expander/gate on every strip [R1]; FCP Expander,
  Noise Gate and Spectral Gate [F4].
- **Why:** gain lifts the floor (to around −36 dBFS here). An expander
  pulls the pauses down without touching the speech, and it handles
  non-steady room noise that a spectral reducer can't learn.
- **Feasibility:** `AUDynamicsProcessor` has an expansion ratio and
  threshold [AD4]. A stage written beside the compressor reuses its
  envelope follower.
- **Flags:** none named. **NG-AU?** if built on `AUDynamicsProcessor`.

**A6. De-esser.**

- **Who:** Resolve [R1]; FCP DeEsser 2 [F4]; Premiere DeEss and DeEsser
  [P5].
- **Why:** EQ presence and heavy compression, both needed for quiet voices,
  bring sibilance forward. For this file it is inconclusive (§2).
- **Feasibility:** no Apple de-esser unit was found. Either a
  side-chain-filtered compressor in `AudioDSP`, or `AUMultiBandCompressor`
  (four bands) [AD5].
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ** (a de-esser is a dynamic EQ).

**A7. Hum removal: a notch at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics.**

- **Who:** FCP Hum Removal [F1]; Premiere DeHum, DeHummer and Notch Filter
  [P5, P7]; Resolve de-hummer [R1].
- **Why:** ground-loop hum from USB and laptop chargers is common in
  desktop setups. A notch removes it surgically where a spectral reducer
  smears. Not indicated for this file (§2).
- **Feasibility:** band-stop filters at f0 and its multiples:
  `AVAudioUnitEQ`'s band-stop type [AD7], or biquads in the tap.
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ**.

**A8. Live loudness metering, and a per-clip loudness readout.**

- **Who:** Resolve loudness meters and graph [R1]; FCP MultiMeter (LUFS,
  true peak) [F5]; Premiere Loudness Meter [P8].
- **Why:** mixing to a target needs momentary, short-term and integrated
  LUFS and true peak while playing, not only after export.
- **Feasibility:** K-weighting and gating already exist (`Loudness.swift`).
  The metering build already reads every track's tap and applies the plan's
  envelope (`AudioTap.swift`, `LevelMeter.swift`).
- **Flags:** none.

**A9. Animate every audio parameter, and draw volume on the clip.**

- **What:** pan, EQ and effect parameters over time, plus a rubber-band
  volume line on the waveform.
- **Who:** Resolve automation of "virtually any control" [R1]; FCP's Audio
  Animation editor [F11]; Premiere clip and track keyframes with the Pen
  tool, and automation modes [P10, P11]; Camtasia audio points [T2].
- **Why:** a static pan or EQ per clip is a creator-tier limit. Professional
  mixes ride levels inside clips, and Frame Job's actions can't reach pan
  or effects today (audio.md).
- **Feasibility:** core and UI work with no new framework. The tap already
  schedules settings by clip span (`AudioDSPSpan`); per-parameter envelopes
  would extend that schedule.
- **Flags:** none.

**A10. Split edits (J- and L-cuts) that keep sync, and reversible
detaching.**

- **Who:** FCP Expand Audio and split edits [F10]; Premiere Unlink and
  ⌥-drag [P16].
- **Why:** J- and L-cuts are the most common dialogue edit. Frame Job's
  Detach Audio is one way, and "no control … switches a clip's audio back
  on" (audio.md).
- **Feasibility:** a model and timeline-gesture change; no framework
  needed.
- **Flags:** none.

**A11. Stems: each track, or each group of tracks, as its own file.**

- **Who:** FCP roles as separate files or a multitrack QuickTime [F9];
  Descript per-track mono files (an article title only) [D4]. Resolve and
  Premiere were not verified.
- **Why:** hand-off to a mixer, music-and-effects versions, a
  voice-without-music version for translation.
- **Feasibility:** per-track files can reuse the export with the other
  tracks silenced. A multitrack MOV would need several `AVAssetWriterInput`s
  (unverified here).
- **Flags:** **NG-ROLES** only if it is done by role rather than by track.

**A12. Track faders and track or bus processing.**

- **Who:** Resolve's mixer, buses and FlexBus [R1]; Premiere's Audio Track
  Mixer and submixes [P10]. FCP gets by without a mixer, through roles and
  compound clips [F3, F8].
- **Why:** "music 6 dB down everywhere" is one fader, not forty clip edits.
  A compressor or limiter across a whole voice track behaves differently
  from per-clip ones at clip boundaries.
- **Feasibility:** a track fader is an envelope in the plan. Track effects
  have no natural home, because composition audio tracks are not timeline
  tracks (`AudioTap.swift` notes the A/B assignment). They need a design
  spike.
- **Flags:** **NG-BUS**.

**A13. 24-bit (and float-decoded) audio export.**

- **Who:** not verified across editors.
- **Why:** a delivery and archival expectation.
- **Feasibility:** issue #86 has the design: a float decode before the gain,
  then an `audio_bits` override.
- **Flags:** none.

### Tier B: expected by the creator and screencast audience

**B1. A one-click "Enhance voice" chain.** **Mic: second.**

- **What:** high-pass → noise reduction or isolation → compressor set
  relative to the clip's measured level → limiter → loudness target. It
  writes ordinary clip settings that a person can then edit.
- **Who:** FCP Enhance Audio [F1]; Resolve AI Audio Assistant (Studio)
  [R2]; Premiere Auto Tag plus Auto-Match [P15, P3]; Descript Studio Sound
  [D1].
- **Why:** a screencaster wants one button. The shipped compressor shows
  that defaults fixed in dBFS fail on a quiet mic (§2).
- **Feasibility:** no DSP beyond A1–A5. The assistant and agents get it
  through the same tool (agent parity).
- **Flags:** inherits its parts' flags.

**B2. Speech-aware ducking.**

- **What:** keyed by voice activity, not clip extent, with a pre-roll. It
  is drawn as an envelope the person can see and edit.
- **Who:** Premiere Auto Ducking, which writes keyframes [P4]; Resolve's
  signal-keyed Ducker with lookahead [R3, R4].
- **Why:** today's ducking holds music down through every pause of a long
  voice clip (audio.md).
- **Feasibility:** the on-device voice model already runs per media for
  Remove Silences (`cleanup-tools.md`). Its speech spans can shape the duck
  envelope in the plan, deterministically, with no new framework.
- **Flags:** none.

**B3. Dialogue leveller (a slow gain rider).**

- **Who:** Resolve Dialogue Leveler [R2, R3].
- **Why:** a speaker who leans in and out, or a two-person recording. Not
  indicated for this file, whose LRA is the pauses (§2).
- **Feasibility:** computed offline from short-term loudness into the
  envelope, or a slow stage of Frame Job's own.
- **Flags:** none.

**B4. De-reverb.**

- **Who:** Premiere Reduce Reverb and DeReverb [P5, P7]; Descript Studio
  Sound "echo" [D1]; Resolve's Dialogue Separator ambience [R3].
- **Why:** laptop microphones in untreated rooms.
- **Feasibility:** no Apple de-reverb unit was found. Whether
  `AUSoundIsolation` removes reverberation is unverified.
- **Flags:** **NG-AU?** if it rides on A4.

**B5. Audio scrubbing.**

- **Who:** FCP audio skimming [F14].
- **Why:** finding a word by ear while dragging the playhead. Frame Job's
  scrub is silent (`timeline.md`).
- **Feasibility:** unverified. It needs short-grain playback at the scrub
  position.
- **Flags:** none.

**B6. Match one clip to another: EQ, level and room.**

- **Who:** FCP Match Audio [F2]; Resolve AI EQ Matcher, Level Matcher and
  Dialogue Matcher [R2].
- **Why:** a camera's scratch audio cut against the RØDE, or two sessions
  on different days.
- **Feasibility:** a spectrum difference becomes an EQ curve (needs A3). The
  level half is A2.
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ**.

**B7. Channel selection: left only, right only, dual mono.**

- **Who:** FCP channel configuration [F7]; Premiere Modify ▸ Audio Channels
  [P12]; Resolve channel mapping [R1, R4]; ScreenFlow per-channel pan and
  level [S1].
- **Why:** USB and XLR interfaces often record a mono mic onto one channel
  of a stereo file. Frame Job's Mix to mono averages the channels, which
  lands 6 dB down when one channel is silent.
- **Feasibility:** a channel pick before the mono fold in the tap. Trivial
  DSP, plus a model field.
- **Flags:** none.

**B8. Clean-up at record time.**

- **Who:** Resolve's Voiceover tool, with Voice Isolation, Dialog Leveler
  and Stereo Fixer while recording [R2]; Descript Studio Sound while
  recording [D1].
- **Why:** a voice-over should land ready to use.
- **Feasibility:** the raw file is kept, and the B1 chain is applied as
  clip settings when the Microphone clip lands, so no new DSP. Apple's
  voice processing on the input node [AD12] was not evaluated and is not
  proposed.
- **Flags:** none.

**B9. Fade and crossfade curve shapes.**

- **Who:** FCP Linear, S-curve, +3 dB and −3 dB [F13]; Premiere Constant
  Gain, Constant Power and Exponential [P18].
- **Feasibility:** envelope shapes in the core's plan.
- **Flags:** none.

**B10. Voice effects (E8).**

- **Who:** FCP Pitch Shifter, Vocal Transformer and reverbs [F4]; Resolve
  Voice Convert (Studio) [R2]; Camtasia Pitch (Mac) [T1]; Descript's
  creative effects [D2]; CapCut voice changer (*unverified*) [C1].
- **Feasibility:** already designed and measured as E8 (#123): fixed chains
  of Apple units rendered offline.
- **Flags:** **E8**; **NG-AU?**

### Tier C: nice to have

| Gap | Who | Feasibility (one line) | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1 Beat detection** (snap edits to beats) | Resolve AI Beat Detector (Studio) [R2]; FCP 12.0 [F16]; CapCut (*unverified*) [C1] | No Apple beat API found; Frame Job's own onset and tempo analysis, cached per media like the sync features | — |
| **C2 Music retimed to a length** | Premiere Remix [P13]; Resolve AI Music Editor (Studio) [R2] | Builds on C1: beat-aligned cuts plus crossfades | — |
| **C3 Source separation** (dialogue, background and ambience; music stems) | Resolve Dialogue Separator, Music Remixer (Studio) [R3] | Apple's `AUAudioMix` (macOS 26) separates foreground and background but reads "Remix metadata from the file asset" [AD2], i.e. Spatial Audio captures, not arbitrary files | NG-AU? |
| **C4 AI speech** (text-to-speech, word regeneration, voice conversion) | Descript Regenerate, AI Speakers [D5]; Resolve Voice Convert [R2], speech generator (21) [R5] | Cloud, so bring-your-own key and no relay; cloning a voice raises consent questions | — |
| **C5 Audio Unit plug-in hosting** | FCP [F3]; Resolve (VST, AU) [R1]; ScreenFlow [S1] | `AVAudioUnitComponentManager` lists installed units [AD11]; hosting live in the tap is the hard part (#123: the tap can't host a pitch shifter); offline render works | NG-AU, NG-PLUGIN |
| **C6 Round-trip to an external audio editor** | Premiere → Audition [P14]; Resolve → external tools such as iZotope RX [R1] | Render a clip's window to WAV and relink the edited return | — |
| **C7 Automatic audio-type tagging** (dialogue, music, effects) | Premiere Auto Tag [P15] | Sound Analysis's built-in classifier ("hundreds of sounds") [AD8]; it would feed B1 and B2 | NG-ROLES if it becomes roles |
| **C8 Spectrum analyzer** | Resolve Frequency Analyzer, RTA [R3]; FCP MultiMeter analyzer [F5] | vDSP FFT on the metering tap (`RealFFT.swift` already exists) | — |
| **C9 Sample-level waveform repair** (pencil, de-click) | Resolve [R1] | Destructive edits to a cached copy; a large UI piece | — |
| **C10 Surround and immersive mixing; ADR tooling** | Resolve [R1, R2]; FCP 5.1 [F7] | Outside the screencast audience | — |

## 6. Sample recordings to add

The owner asked for more real recordings. Each one below is chosen to give a
gap a "before" to measure against. Keep each 30–90 s, record at the device's
native rate, and add a `samples/README.md` row measured the way
`Rode-usb-mic.m4a`'s was: true peak, integrated LUFS, LRA, plus the measure
named here.

| # | Recording | Exercises | Measure for the README row |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The same RØDE, the same words, mouth about 10 cm from the mic with the gain up, including a laugh or shout that **clips** | A1, A2; what clipping at the source does to them (de-clipping was not surveyed) | Sample peak at 0 dBFS, count of full-scale samples |
| 2 | Desk mic with a **fan, HVAC or laptop-charger hum** audible in the pauses | A7, A4, the shipped noise reducer, A5 | Tonal peak at 50/60 Hz and its harmonics over neighbouring bins; floor in dBFS |
| 3 | A **sibilant** voice close to the mic (lines dense in "s", "sh", "ch") | A6, and A3's presence boost making it worse | 5–9 kHz vs 0.3–4 kHz ratio, 95th percentile |
| 4 | The **MacBook's built-in mic** in a hard-walled room, 1 m away | A4, B4 | The decay after a hand clap (a reverb time estimate) |
| 5 | **Plosives**: "p" and "b" lines close to a mic with no pop filter | A3 high-pass | Energy below 80 Hz on the plosive windows |
| 6 | **Two people, two mics**, a conversation with cross-talk and bleed (two files) | A5, B2, B3, A12, Synchronize Audio | LRA per file; bleed level of one voice on the other's mic |
| 7 | A voice-over with **pauses over a music bed** (two files, voice and music) | B2, A8, A11, C1, C2 | Music's integrated LUFS; voice's speech spans |
| 8 | A speaker who **moves off-mic** and back (turning away mid-sentence) | B3 | Short-term loudness spread over speech-only windows |
| 9 | A **stereo file with the mic on one channel only** (a USB or XLR interface's input 1) | B7 | Per-channel peak; the silent channel's floor |
| 10 | A **screen recording with system audio** (app sounds, a notification ding) **and the mic** | A12, A11, B2 | Per-file integrated LUFS |
| 11 | The **GH5's camera audio and the RØDE**, the same take | B6, A2, Synchronize Audio | Integrated LUFS and spectral tilt of each |
| 12 | An **iPhone video with Spatial Audio** capture (the owner's iPhone) | C3: does `AUAudioMix` read its remix metadata | Whether the asset carries the metadata; separation result |
| 13 | A **10-minute** talking-head take on the RØDE | Offline render time and cache size for A4 and B1; A2 on long material | Duration; render time per minute when built |

1	# Spec §11 — decisions: Audio (the owner's audio pass, from 2026-10-30)
2	
3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
4	[`README.md`](README.md).
5	
6	The owner's pass over a clip's sound, begun 2026-10-30 to turn a desktop USB microphone's
7	recording into usable audio for a video. Its IDs are the AU- series. Each was recorded before
8	its code.
9	
10	- **AU-1 — `audio.volume`'s ceiling is ×32 (+30.1 dB), not ×4; the Volume slider keeps its
11	  0–400 % travel and the field beside it takes the rest (owner, 2026-10-30: "400% should not be
12	  a hard max").** The owner's recording `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a` (a RØDE USB microphone,
13	  30.4 s of AAC mono at 48 kHz) peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated loudness of −44.7 LUFS
14	  (ffmpeg's `volumedetect` and `ebur128`), so Normalize wanted ×7.55 to reach −1 dBFS and stopped
15	  at ×4, −6.5 dBFS. The ceiling stays — `MAX_GAIN` still bounds `check_audio`'s refusal,

Found by road map "audio" AP6c (Enhance the microphone when it lands), landed in f36ace3; the review asked for it to be filed.

`tools/proof/audio_ap6_proof.py` V8 launches its instance with `-FrameJobNormalizeTargetLUFS -16`. A bare `-16` is read by the argument domain as a flag, so the value never reaches `UserDefaults` (AP6c confirmed this with a small test binary while writing `audio_ap6c_proof.py` V4, which passes `'<real>-18</real>'` instead).

Today this is harmless: −16 is Normalize's default, so V8 measures what it means to. But the row does not test what it says, and a change of the default, or a copy of the line with another target, would silently measure the wrong thing.

Fix: pass `'<real>-16</real>'` as V8's value (as V4 of `audio_ap6c_proof.py` does), and re-run `audio_ap6_proof.py` against Release.

Found while verifying road map "audio" AP5 (commit 33750bd).

Either say in the row's failure text how to make a baseline from the right build, or carry the baseline.

content.content:
Found while proving road map "audio" AP6b (the leveller), integrated in `bc885e9` on `worktree-audio-updates`.

## What happens

After `play_preview` seeks (any play not from where the stream starts), `MTAudioProcessingTapGetSourceAudio` hands each tap buffers whose `timeRange.duration` is zero (0/48000) and whose samples are silent (peak 0.0), but whose `timeRange.start` is the seek's frame. On a seek to 20 s: two of 4096 frames at 960000, then real audio from 963072 (logged per buffer on a Debug build, 2026-10-31).

`AudioTapContext.process` places the first of them in the live meter's ring (`meter.capture`, guarded only by a numeric time), so `LiveLoudness` sums 4096 frames of silence at [960000, 964096) and drops the overlap of what follows. Replacing those frames of the export with silence reproduces the meter's reading to four places (−23.2635 LUFS, against the export's −23.2532 over the same frames).

The first play after a build is exact, because the player's first filler carries an invalid time (`0/0`), which the capture already skips.

## How big

The error depends on the material at the seek:
- the off-mic fixture unprocessed, 12 s from 0 then 7 s from 25 s (loud speech): ΔI −0.0385 and −0.0398 LU;
- from 20 s (a quiet segment under the relative gate): 0.0000;
- levelled (the quiet segment lifted), 8 s from 20 s: −0.0102 LU on Release, −0.0041 on Debug;
- a constant pan −0.5 from 25 s (an earlier session): 0.0160.

## Tried and not kept

Not capturing a buffer whose duration is zero or invalid (a `sourced:` argument to `AudioTapContext.process`, false when `timeRange.duration` is zero or not numeric, and `guard sourced, …` before `meter.capture`) makes both seeks read 0.0000 and `audio_ap7_proof.py`'s L2 pass. But L3 (two plays of 2 s back to back, AU-72's pause and continue) then resets on the resume — "resets 4, 4, 5; from 48896 then 144511" — because the real audio resumes 5375 frames past the frame the sum reached at the pause, a gap the filler used to bridge. So the fix needs the resume path settled with it: what a resume's filler carries, and whether the frames between the sum's last tick and the pause were heard.

On the base's code the same Debug instance's `audio_ap7_proof.py` live rows read 2/4 (L2 "resets 2 -> 4", L3 "resets 5, 6, 6", one run).

## Where it shows now

AP6b's P3 (`tools/proof/audio_ap6b_proof.py`) subtracts a control — the levelled export played as a clip of its own — so the row holds the leveller's own part (spec §11 AU-67 (e)). With this fixed, the row could be absolute again.

# Frame Job — design and implementation spec

**The normative spec, one file per section.** It was one 4,780-line file,
`designs/reelcut-design.md`, until 2026-09-26 (git history has it). Section numbers are
unchanged, so a citation like "spec §7.3" is `07.3-frame-recipe.md` and "spec §11 W-8" is found
through [`11-decisions/README.md`](11-decisions/README.md).

**Never read the whole spec.** Read this index, then only the file for the section you need.
For a decision, look its ID up in `11-decisions/README.md`, or grep this directory
(`grep -rn "W-8 —" designs/spec/`). A file that grows past ~500 lines splits by subsection into
lettered files that keep its number (§4.3 is `04.3a`, `04.3b` and `04.3c`, §5.2 is `05.2a` and `05.2b`, §6 is `06a`, `06b` and `06c`, §7.5 is `07.5a` and `07.5b`, §7.9 is `07.9a`, `07.9b`, `07.9c` and `07.9d`);
a citation of the bare number names them together, and this index gets their rows in the same
change. Until #342 (2026-10-24) §4.3b was the Media, Document and Assistant tabs, now §4.3c; an older citation of §4.3b (in `archive/` or git history) means §4.3c.

The Lines column is `wc -l`; the `11-decisions/` cell is that folder's total, its README
included, and `make test` checks both (`tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py`).

| File | Lines | Read it for |
|---|---|---|
| [`01-what-this-is.md`](01-what-this-is.md) | 47 | The product in one page, its opening flow, and its non-goals. |
| [`02-six-ideas.md`](02-six-ideas.md) | 26 | The six ideas the model is built on, and why it stays simple. |
| [`03-window-layout.md`](03-window-layout.md) | 71 | The window's regions, as the design handoff specifies them. |
| **§4 — The regions in detail** | | |
| [`04.1-toolbar.md`](04.1-toolbar.md) | 25 | The toolbar. |
| [`04.2-preview-canvas.md`](04.2-preview-canvas.md) | 171 | The preview canvas: selection, handles, crop and region modes, on-canvas text, snapping, Show Ungraded and the scopes panel (its two slots, their sizes and the four scopes drawn). |
| [`04.3a-inspector-clip-tab.md`](04.3a-inspector-clip-tab.md) | 141 | The inspector's tab strip and its Clip tab: the sub-tabs and pinned block, the selection header and name field, sections, row marks, Reset/Clear, the note on the section list, and the controls the sections use (Rasterize's `OptionControls`). |
| [`04.3b-inspector-clip-sections.md`](04.3b-inspector-clip-sections.md) | 520 | The Clip tab's sections: every video, audio, text and shape section. |
| [`04.3c-inspector-media-document-assistant.md`](04.3c-inspector-media-document-assistant.md) | 228 | The inspector's Media tab (find band, rows, drags, Consolidate, import), the File menu's caption commands (Import, Generate and Export Captions), the Document tab and the Assistant tab. |
| [`04.4-timeline.md`](04.4-timeline.md) | 275 | The timeline: its bar, the level meter, ruler, tracks, clip bodies, gestures, entering a nest. |
| **§5 — Editing model** | | |
